stories.headline: Microsoft declares 'Code Red' to overhaul reliability after 24-hour cloud outage
stories.dek: Internal memos reviewed by Reuters set a target of one-hour worldwide resolution of future incidents and describe engineers struggling to coordinate during the November 12-13 failure.
stories.summary: Microsoft has declared a 'Code Red', its most urgent internal alert, to rework how it prevents and handles major service failures, according to memos reviewed by Reuters. The move follows a nearly 24-hour outage on November 12-13 that hit Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams and Copilot.
body: Microsoft has declared a 'Code Red' to overhaul its engineering and crisis-response practices after a nearly 24-hour outage on November 12-13, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters.

The company's own description of the alert is that it is the highest level of urgency. The outage disrupted Exchange Online, Microsoft's cloud-based email service, along with Outlook, Teams, the Copilot AI assistant and other Microsoft 365 products. Reuters reported that it affected governments from Australia and Japan to the United States, delayed trading firms and disrupted airline communications.

Microsoft blamed an undetected defect in Windows, related to how the software handles growth in demand, that was introduced in July. It said the incident was not related to cyber activity or AI agents. Chief executive Satya Nadella publicly apologised for the disruption.

Jason Henderson, president of M365 Core, said in a memo to staff on Friday that it was the most customer-impacting incident in the history of Exchange Online. "Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team," he wrote. He added: "Unfortunately, all the work we have done over the years was not sufficient to protect us on Thursday."

Amanda Silver, a corporate vice president overseeing M365 Core and Work IQ, said in a separate memo on Monday that engineers worked through a "fog of war". Responders exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats, she said, and struggled to keep a shared picture of hypotheses and decisions because diagnostic data sat in fragmented internal tracking systems.

Silver's memo quotes Charles Lamanna, executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, telling a Code Red review that the affected component had experienced "roughly ten years' worth of acceptable failures."

Silver outlined five workstreams. They centre on load shedding (dropping some demand so a strained system keeps running), geographic traffic partitioning (keeping traffic in separate regions so a fault does not spread) and faster recovery mechanisms.

Microsoft has set a target of resolving future incidents worldwide within an hour. It plans to use AI agents to help engineers read system-health data more quickly. Henderson will hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team, which oversees the engineering group behind the underlying Microsoft 365 services, plus weekly reviews.

In an earlier memo this month, Henderson said urgent patches to M365 Core took too long to deploy worldwide. In one recent incident, he wrote, an urgent production fix took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. For the most urgent security issues, he said, the goal is an hour from detection to safe worldwide deployment. "Needless to say, we aren't here yet," he wrote.

A Microsoft spokesperson told Reuters the company's teams keep working around the clock to apply lessons learned after service is restored. Ars Technica noted that Microsoft has not said when it expects to meet the one-hour targets.
keyFacts: The outage ran from November 12 to 13 and lasted nearly 24 hours.
Microsoft blamed an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July.
Responders exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats.
Microsoft targets one-hour worldwide resolution of future incidents; no date given.
In one recent incident, an urgent fix took five to six days to reach all users.
stories.background: Microsoft 365 is the company's bundle of workplace software, including email, Teams and Office applications. Substrate is the engineering group responsible for its underlying services. Microsoft said the November outage was not caused by a cyberattack or by AI tools.
stories.whyItMatters: Businesses, governments and airlines relying on Microsoft 365 were affected by the outage. The memos set out the speed targets Microsoft says it wants to meet in future incidents.

stories.headline: Centre allots Lutyens' Delhi bungalow to Dalai Lama's office, sources say
stories.dek: The allotment to Gaden Phodrang Trust followed a request from the external affairs ministry, but the housing ministry has not commented officially.
stories.summary: The Centre has allotted a Type-7 bungalow on Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Lane in Lutyens' Delhi to the Dalai Lama's office, Gaden Phodrang Trust, sources said. Members of the Tibetan parliament-in-exile welcomed the decision.
body: The central government has allotted a bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi to the Dalai Lama and his office, Gaden Phodrang Trust, sources told news outlets on Tuesday.

The house is a Type-7 bungalow on Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Lane, according to The Times of India. There has been no official word from the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry, whose officials did not respond to the newspaper's queries.

Sources said the allotment was made after a request from the Ministry of External Affairs. The Times of India reported that the housing ministry had transferred the bungalow to the external affairs ministry last year. People aware of the matter said such accommodation is usually transferred for three years and can be extended.

Members of the Tibetan parliament-in-exile welcomed the move. Speaker Dolma Tsering, quoted by the news agency ANI, called it "very welcome news". She said the accommodation would make the Dalai Lama's visits to the capital more convenient and more comfortable.

Choedak Gyatso, a member of the parliament-in-exile and of its standing committee, said: "government of India has given us refuge when we had no country. We lost our country, and it gave us Dharamshala when we had no land and gave us schools and many institutions that can preserve our culture."
Gyatso said he had visited the bungalow with the Tibetan deputy speaker during a recent official trip to Delhi, and called it a great honour.

Gaden Phodrang was registered as a private trust in India in 2011, after the Dalai Lama relinquished political authority in favour of an elected Tibetan leadership. Its website says the trust works to preserve the institution of the Dalai Lama and advance his humanitarian vision. The website lists among his commitments the promotion of human values, interfaith harmony, the preservation of Tibetan culture and identity, environmental protection and a deeper appreciation of ancient Indian wisdom.
keyFacts: The bungalow is a Type-7 house on Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Lane, Lutyens' Delhi.
It was allotted to Gaden Phodrang Trust, the Dalai Lama's office.

stories.headline: Centre plans multi-year motor insurance, 'no insurance, no fuel' pilot at 10 pumps
stories.dek: A Supreme Court committee has asked two ministries to trial fuel refusal for uninsured vehicles at five pumps each in Haryana and Uttar Pradesh.
stories.summary: The road transport ministry is proposing a single premium for multi-year third-party policies for cars and two-wheelers, and linking premiums to traffic offences. A 'no insurance, no fuel' pilot is proposed at ten petrol pumps in the NCR.
body: The road transport ministry is proposing a single premium for four-year and six-year insurance policies for cars and two-wheelers respectively, as part of measures to reduce the number of uninsured vehicles, The Times of India reported.

Separately, the Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety has asked the road transport and petroleum ministries to start a 'no insurance, no fuel' pilot. It would run at five petrol pumps each in Haryana and Uttar Pradesh. The selected pumps have automated number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras, which can identify vehicles and help check their insurance status.

The newspaper also learnt that the ministry is working on a plan to link premiums to traffic offences recorded against a vehicle owner in the previous year. Under the proposal, premiums could rise based on specific violations, so repeat offenders would pay more.
The ministry is also examining revisions to base insurance rates for certain vehicle categories, including electric vehicles, as part of a wider review of the current premium structure.
The changes are meant to encourage more owners to keep valid insurance and to improve compliance with the Motor Vehicles Act.

Insurance data show nearly 25 crore active vehicles have valid cover, about 81% of vehicles currently running in the country. More than 90% of heavy commercial vehicles are insured, against around 88% of cars and around 80% of two-wheelers. Compliance is lowest among three-wheelers, at around 57%.

The Supreme Court had earlier directed the government to examine ways of ensuring that vehicles on roads have valid insurance. The proposals have not been announced officially, and the report did not give a start date for the pilot.

stories.whyItMatters: Vehicles without valid insurance can leave accident victims and their families with inadequate compensation, the report said. Owners with repeated traffic violations could face higher premiums under the proposal.

stories.headline: Delhi records season's coldest morning at 10°C; air quality stays 'poor'
stories.dek: The minimum at Safdarjung was 1.3 degrees below normal, and the IMD forecasts mist or shallow fog in Delhi-NCR and dense fog at isolated places in the Northeast.
stories.summary: Delhi recorded its coldest morning of the season on Wednesday, with a minimum of 10 degrees Celsius at Safdarjung. The average AQI was 224, in the 'poor' category, and the IMD forecast shallow fog and a maximum near 25 degrees.
body: Delhi recorded its coldest morning of the season on Wednesday, with the minimum temperature at Safdarjung, the city's base weather station, settling at 10 degrees Celsius, NDTV reported.
The reading was 1.3 degrees below the season's normal and 1.2 degrees lower than on Tuesday. Lodhi Road recorded 10.1 degrees, Ayanagar 10.4 degrees, Palam 11 degrees and the Ridge 11.7 degrees.

Palam's minimum was unchanged from Tuesday. Lodhi Road fell by 0.6 degrees and the Ridge by 0.3 degrees, while Ayanagar rose by 0.2 degrees. No rainfall was recorded at any of the five weather stations in the 24 hours ending at 8.30 am.

Air quality stayed in the 'poor' category. The city's average Air Quality Index stood at 224, with four monitoring stations recording 'very poor' readings. Under Central Pollution Control Board categories, 201 to 300 is 'poor' and 301 to 400 is 'very poor'.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast shallow fog for Wednesday, with the maximum temperature likely to reach 25 degrees Celsius.

For Thursday, November 26, the IMD expects mainly clear skies in Delhi and no rain over the next few days, according to The Times of India. Mist or shallow fog is likely in the morning, with moderate fog at isolated places. The department said foggy conditions could become more widespread towards the end of its five-day forecast period, potentially reducing visibility across Delhi-NCR.

Elsewhere, the IMD has warned of dense fog at isolated places over Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura. Rajasthan, Punjab and Haryana are expected to stay dry, and no rainfall warnings have been issued for them.
Rain is forecast for parts of the Northeast and Lakshadweep. India TV News reported on Tuesday that the speed limit on the Yamuna Expressway was reduced from 100 to 75 kmph because of winter fog.

stories.headline: IMD forecasts heavy rain for Tamil Nadu, Kerala as northeast monsoon strengthens
stories.dek: The weather office also warned of dense fog across Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi, and said minimum temperatures will fall in central and east India.
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department forecast isolated heavy rain over Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal through November 27, with gusty winds in the south. One education outlet said schools may close this week; the IMD forecast carries no closure order.
body: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast isolated heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal through November 27, citing easterly waves, troughs in the easterlies and upper air cyclonic circulations.

In Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, isolated to scattered rain is likely to continue until November 30. Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds of 40–50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, are expected through November 28.

Kerala and Mahe are likely to see fairly widespread to widespread rain through November 28, followed by isolated to scattered showers on November 29 and 30. Winds of 30–40 kmph, gusting to 50 kmph, are forecast through November 27.

Lakshadweep is expected to receive fairly widespread to widespread rain from November 25 to 29. Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema may see isolated to scattered rain through November 30, with strong surface winds through November 28.
Coastal Karnataka and South Interior Karnataka are likely to get isolated to scattered rain through November 28. Telangana may see isolated to scattered rain on November 25.

Headlines from regional outlets said the northeast monsoon had gained strength in Tamil Nadu, with heavy rain forecast for the delta and southern districts. Education Times reported that schools could close this week because of the alert. The full texts of those reports were not available, and the IMD forecast reviewed here contains no closure orders.

In the north, the IMD warned of dense fog at night and in the morning. Punjab is covered through November 27, Himachal Pradesh through November 26, and Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi from November 26 to 27.

The IMD said fog could disrupt airports, highways and railways, lengthen journeys and trip power lines. It advised commuters to drive cautiously, use fog lights and check schedules with airlines, railways and state transport. People with asthma or bronchitis were advised to avoid going out unless necessary and to cover their faces.

For Delhi, the IMD forecast mainly clear skies with mist or shallow fog in the morning. Maximum temperatures on November 25 and 26 are likely to be 24°C to 26°C and minimums 9°C to 11°C, both below normal at most places. On November 27, minimums may fall to 8°C–10°C.

Minimum temperatures in central India are likely to fall by 2–4°C through November 25. In east India, a fall of 3–4°C is expected through November 26. No significant change is expected elsewhere this week.

stories.headline: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, hits 204 off 53 balls as India A beat UAE
stories.dek: The left-hander set List A records for the fastest hundred, 150 and double-century, and for most sixes in an innings, with 28.
stories.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, scored 204 off 53 balls for India A against the UAE in the Rising Stars Asia Cup in Doha on Tuesday. India A chased 250 in 14.2 overs to win by seven wickets.
body: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, scored 204 off 53 balls for India A against the UAE in Doha on Tuesday, setting List A records for the fastest century and double-century as India A won the Rising Stars Asia Cup match by seven wickets.

India A chased the target of 250 in 14.2 overs, finishing on 254 for 3 with 214 balls remaining. Sooryavanshi hit seven fours and 28 sixes, a strike rate of 384.90. ESPNcricinfo and The Guardian reported the 28 sixes as the most in a senior men's innings. The win took India A into the semifinals, according to The Hindu.

He reached his hundred off 28 balls, one fewer than the 29 taken by Australia's Jake Fraser-McGurk in 2023. His 150 came off 40 balls, bettering his own record, and his 200 off 52 balls. The previous fastest List A double-century was Chad Bowes's 200 off 103 balls for Canterbury against Otago in 2024.

Sooryavanshi began the chase with two dot balls, then hit three successive sixes off Zahid Ali and reached fifty off 16 balls. Wicketkeeper Aftab Alam missed a stumping chance when he was on 76, and a catch was dropped at deep cover when he was on 163. He was out in the 13th over, caught at long-off while attempting another six, with India A five runs short of victory.

Ibrar Ahmad finished with figures of 3-0-71-1 after Sooryavanshi took 6, 4, 4, 6, 6, 4 off one over. India A captain Tilak Varma said after the match: "No words to say for him. I would only say it's like absolute carnage."

In a video released by the BCCI, Sooryavanshi said he had spoken to Yuvraj Singh for almost half an hour the night before, after struggling in his first two matches in the tournament. "He explained everything to me well and said that if I played 20 balls, the score would be different," he said.
UAE had batted first and made 249 for 8. Harpreet Singh scored 130 off 144 balls, his career-best List A score. Arshad Khan took 4 for 43 for India A.
keyFacts: Sooryavanshi scored 204 off 53 balls, with seven fours and 28 sixes.

His 200 came off 52 balls; the previous record was 103 balls by Chad Bowes.

stories.background: Sooryavanshi became India's youngest men's international in July, when he made his T20I debut against England in Manchester. He scored 776 runs for Rajasthan Royals in this year's IPL, the most in the tournament, at a strike rate of 237.30. He had modest returns in his first two matches at the Rising Stars Asia Cup.

stories.headline: Gukesh draws game 1 of world title match with Sindarov despite time trouble
stories.dek: The defending champion, playing black, held the Uzbek challenger to a repetition draw in 38 moves at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny.
stories.summary: Defending world champion Gukesh Dommaraju drew the opening game of his title match against Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva on Tuesday, after running short of time. The game ended by repetition after 38 moves; game 2 is on Wednesday.
body: Defending world champion Gukesh Dommaraju drew the first game of his 14-game title match against Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov on Tuesday, surviving a long battle against the clock at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, near Geneva.

Gukesh, playing black, chose the Berlin Defence to the Ruy Lopez. The queens came off the board on the eighth move, and Sindarov steered the game into less familiar territory with 13 Ne4, according to The Guardian.

The Hindu reported that Gukesh was behind on the clock for most of the game. At one stage he had to make 22 moves in 24 minutes, and later had about six minutes for nine moves. The Guardian said he spent more than 36 minutes on a single move, and nearly an hour combined on his 13th and 17th moves.
The game reached a same-coloured-bishop ending and finished by repetition of moves, with 38 played in all. Sindarov later took more time himself after earlier moving quickly, The Hindu said.

Gukesh said the time he invested early helped him later. "When I got into the time trouble, I'd already thought about the next few moves," he said. "And then the moves after that were pretty easy." He also said: "It wasn't in a place where I really needed to be worried."
Sindarov said he had tried to push at every moment because of his advantage on the clock. "But Gukesh defended well in the end," he said.
Gukesh plays white in game 2 on Wednesday. The match is the best of 14 games, and the first player to reach 7½ points wins the title.
keyFacts: Game 1 ended in a draw by repetition after 38 moves on Tuesday.

stories.background:
Gukesh became the youngest undisputed world champion in December 2024 by beating China's Ding Liren. Sindarov won this year's Candidates tournament in Cyprus, finishing unbeaten, and won the 2025 Fide World Cup in Goa. Both players are 20.

Each player has 120 minutes for the first 40 moves, then 30 minutes for the rest of the game. A 7-7 score after 14 games would lead to faster tiebreaks on December 12.

stories.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, putting open-weight AI policy in focus
stories.dek: Huang has lobbied Washington to back US-built open-weight models, a position Anthropic's chief executive partly disputes on security grounds.
stories.summary: Nvidia's board said on Monday it would reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive after he resigned over reports of extramarital affairs. His return has drawn attention to a Washington dispute over open-weight AI models and competition with China.
body: Nvidia's board announced on Monday that it would reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, after he resigned following reports of extramarital affairs, including with a woman whom news reports said was suspected of spying for the Chinese government.

Before the scandal, Huang had urged Congress and the Trump administration to support American companies building open-weight AI models. These are models whose core components are made public, so users can download, modify and adapt them for specific tasks. Closed models, by contrast, are sold as access to systems whose underlying technology the developer controls.

People familiar with the matter said on Monday that President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance personally intervened in the board's decision, partly because they saw Huang as a protector of US-made open-weight models. The White House did not comment on that link.

A White House official told Reuters on Tuesday that "the Trump Administration's clear and long-standing policy has been strong support for" open-weight AI models. The administration says such models give startups dependable, cheaper options outside proprietary tools from companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic.
Open-weight models also serve Nvidia's business. They widen demand for its chips and computing infrastructure beyond a small number of leading model developers.

Executives at OpenAI and Anthropic, which earn revenue by selling access to proprietary systems, have expressed scepticism of open-weight models, according to their public statements. In a letter earlier this year, Huang urged the US government to avoid "premature restrictions" on open-weight tools. Andreessen Horowitz, Microsoft and Palantir co-signed it. Anthropic declined.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said he disagreed with parts of Huang's statement. He argued that increasingly capable open-weight models could create security risks, and said "sufficiently capable" AI tools could use publicly available materials to spread infectious diseases.
Luther Lowe of Y Combinator, a startup fund, said "any kind of political headwinds against Huang and Nvidia could be a harbinger for a crackdown on open weights."

China is a central part of the debate. Chinese models such as DeepSeek and Alibaba's offerings have won American business users because they are often cheaper than proprietary systems from OpenAI and Anthropic, while performing comparably on many tasks.

Over the summer, the administration told leading developers it would not put open-weight models through voluntary government safety tests, Reuters reported. It is also considering requiring US companies to disclose their use of Chinese-made AI models, Reuters reported last week.

Last week, House Homeland Security Committee chair Andrew Garbarino and China Committee chair John Moolenaar, both Republicans, urged a ban on Chinese open-weight models in government agencies and contractors. They also want US developers to get more access to computing resources. "The time to act is now, while we still have the opportunity and leverage to do so," they said in a joint statement.

Closed developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic sell access to systems they keep proprietary. Chinese open-weight models, including DeepSeek, now lead the field, according to the reports.
stories.whyItMatters: Decisions on open-weight models affect which AI tools US startups and government contractors can use, and how much regulation US developers face.

stories.headline: Tidal to delete fully AI-generated music from its service on December 9
stories.dek: The streaming service says 43% of tracks uploaded over 90 days were fully AI-made, and it will also block distributors from delivering such songs.
stories.summary: Tidal said on Tuesday it will ban songs generated entirely by AI and begin deleting them on December 9. Outlets report the number of tracks affected as 27 million or around 29 million; music made with AI assistance will still be allowed.
body: Music streaming service Tidal said on Tuesday that it will ban songs generated entirely by artificial intelligence and start deleting them from its catalogue on December 9.

The company said 43 per cent of tracks distributed to it over the past 90 days were detected as fully AI-generated. Tidal's music lead, Robert Andersen, described the earlier steps as insufficient and said on X that "something more drastic" was needed. Ars Technica reported that new uploads reached 60 per cent AI-generated on November 6.

The reports differ on the scale of the deletion. Tidal's figure for tracks currently labelled as AI is 27 million, or 6.3 per cent of its catalogue, according to TechCrunch and Ars Technica. TechCrunch, The Verge and Pitchfork put the total to be removed at around 29 million. TechCrunch said that figure would be reached by the end of the year.

Tidal said 96 per cent of the AI-labelled tracks received no plays in the past 90 days. "We believe this will resonate with both artists and listeners alike, as 96% of all AI-generated songs receive zero plays at all," Andersen said.

After December 9, Tidal expects to reject roughly 80,000 to 85,000 tracks a day. It will also bar distribution services, the companies that deliver music to streaming platforms, from submitting fully AI-generated songs. It will turn away submissions whose metadata says they were made wholly with AI.

The company said it will still accept music made with AI tools, as long as AI is not the sole output. Pitchfork reported that Tidal uses detection software from the French company Ircam Amplify, which advertises 99 per cent accuracy and a 1 per cent false-positive rate. Pitchfork calculated that this could mean close to 290,000 songs wrongly removed, and said it has asked Tidal what recourse artists will have if their music is wrongly flagged.

Tidal said wholly AI-generated music meant to mislead listeners and impersonate artists "diverts streams and royalties away from the artists, and confuses fans." It has already removed about 66,000 tracks for impersonating artists, according to Ars Technica; Pitchfork cited 65,000.

Pitchfork also asked Tidal whether it will keep demonetising music that is substantially, but not wholly, made with AI. Tidal's June policy covered music "wholly or substantially" generated by AI, while the new statement refers only to entirely AI-generated music.

Spotify, YouTube Music and Apple Music have chosen labels, and Deezer is adding a toggle for users to filter out AI music.
stories.whyItMatters: Tidal says AI uploads divert streams and royalty payments from human artists. Artists whose music is wrongly flagged as AI may be affected, and Tidal has not yet said what recourse it will offer.

stories.headline: IT employee groups seek common rules on AI job losses as campus hiring dips
stories.dek: Employee representatives want companies to disclose AI-linked layoffs, while Tamil Nadu colleges report up to 20% fewer IT offers for freshers.
stories.summary: Employee representatives and workforce experts want a common framework requiring IT companies to disclose roles cut because of AI and to offer severance and redeployment. Separately, Tamil Nadu campuses report IT hiring down by up to 20% this year.
body: Employee representatives and workforce experts in India's information technology industry have called for a common framework requiring companies to disclose job losses linked to AI and to protect affected staff, The Economic Times reported on Wednesday.

Under the proposal, companies would track and disclose how many roles were eliminated because of AI, how many employees were moved into other roles and how many were retrained. The proposal also sets minimum standards on severance, advance notice, redeployment and reskilling.
It would expect companies to explore redeployment within the firm before making staff redundant, to provide fair severance, and to support those who need to move to other jobs.

Separately, The Times of India reported that campuses across Tamil Nadu have seen IT hiring fall by up to 20% this year. The newspaper said companies are using AI tools for basic coding and testing tasks, and now look for graduates who can work with AI, check AI-generated code, spot security risks and interpret data.
A senior executive at one of the large IT companies told the newspaper that fresher hiring had declined by more than 20% from last year as coding and testing were automated.

Anna University had placed 498 students in software and product development by November last year and has placed 416 in the same period this year. Across its four campuses it had placed 607 students till November 18, which is 50 fewer than last year.

Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science reported a 10% to 15% dip in IT company offers. VIT said offers were down 5%. Its placement director, V Samuel Rajkumar, said Global Capability Centres, which are companies' India-based units handling work for their parent firms, had cut intake by 20%.

College officials said the change is one of altered roles rather than lost ones. "AI is certainly reshaping entry-level IT hiring, but it is transformation of roles rather than elimination of IT jobs," said Vikas Misra, vice-chancellor of HITS.

Some institutions reported different trends. Sastra said fresher pay had risen, with good candidates getting offers of Rs6 lakh a year instead of Rs4 lakh. RMK Engineering College said its students had received 750 offers, about the same as last year.

Anna University said it plans to train faculty in domain-specific AI skills and has introduced department-specific recruitment drives. Rajkumar said the full effect of AI on campus hiring would be known at the end of the year.

stories.headline: ICMR survey finds 55.9% of non-pregnant women aged 15-49 are anaemic
stories.dek: The SAMPADA survey also found vitamin B12 deficiency in about two-thirds of adolescents, and iron deficiency in only part of anaemia cases.
stories.summary: An ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition survey found anaemia in 55.9 per cent of non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 15-49. It also reported vitamin B12 deficiency in about two-thirds of adolescents.
body: More than half of women of reproductive age in India are anaemic, according to the SAMPADA survey of the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition for 2023-25, which found a prevalence of 55.9 per cent among non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 15-49.

The survey covered more than two lakh people across 183 districts in 35 states and union territories. It drew on data from over 81,000 households and analysed over 1.7 lakh blood samples, The Times of India reported.
Andaman and Nicobar recorded the highest prevalence among that group of women, at 81.2 per cent. State-wise estimates showed sharp regional differences.

Among other groups, anaemia affected 46.3 per cent of adolescent girls and 22.8 per cent of adolescent boys aged 10-19. It was found in 43.6 per cent of pregnant women, 58.1 per cent of lactating women and 22 per cent of men aged 20-59. Among children, the figure was 41.8 per cent for those aged 12-59 months and 31.3 per cent for those aged 5-9 years.
Vitamin B12 deficiency was found in 65.4 per cent of adolescent girls and 66.1 per cent of adolescent boys. It affected 57.4 per cent of women of reproductive age and 60.4 per cent of men aged 20-59.

Iron deficiency accompanied anaemia in only 27 per cent of adolescent girls and women of reproductive age. Iron deficiency itself affected 36.3 per cent of adolescent girls, 34.1 per cent of women of reproductive age and 10 per cent of adolescent boys.

The SAMPADA report noted that about half of anaemic women, adolescent girls and children have mild anaemia, The Hindu reported. The newsletter said the Union Health Ministry claimed rates of severe anaemia have dropped.

Dr Tulika Seth, professor of haematology at AIIMS, said not all anaemia stems from iron, vitamin B12 or folate deficiency. "Conditions such as thalassaemia, sickle cell disease, aplastic anaemia, chronic kidney disease, tuberculosis and cancer can also cause anaemia. Iron supplements alone will not help these patients," she said.
Seth said her team has been working with the Anaemia Mukt Bharat programme to develop simple algorithms to identify such cases.
keyFacts: Anaemia found in 55.9% of non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 15-49.
Andaman and Nicobar had the highest prevalence in that group, at 81.2%.
Vitamin B12 deficiency affected 65.4% of adolescent girls and 66.1% of adolescent boys.
Survey covered 183 districts and analysed over 1.7 lakh blood samples.
stories.background: The NFHS-6 fact sheets released earlier this year did not include anaemia estimates. The government said these would come from an independent ICMR survey using venous blood samples. NFHS-5 had reported 57 per cent prevalence among women aged 15-49, but the two surveys covered different groups and used different testing methods, so the figures are not directly comparable.
stories.whyItMatters: The findings indicate that iron supplements alone may not address anaemia in many women and adolescents, since iron deficiency accompanied anaemia in only 27 per cent of adolescent girls and women of reproductive age.

stories.headline: 69 former officials urge Centre to scrap 1,750 MW Demwe Lower dam in Arunachal
stories.dek: The retired civil servants say the Lohit River project threatens rainforest, wildlife and indigenous communities, and that its approvals ignored expert and tribunal objections.
stories.summary: A group of 69 former bureaucrats has asked the Union environment ministry to drop the proposed Demwe Lower hydroelectric project in Arunachal Pradesh. Their letter of November 23 cites ecological, social and legal concerns.
body: A group of 69 former bureaucrats has urged the Union environment ministry to scrap the proposed 1,750 MW Demwe Lower Hydroelectric Project on the Lohit River in Arunachal Pradesh, citing its likely impact on biodiversity, indigenous communities and the ecology of the eastern Himalayas.

The letter is dated November 23. It is also addressed to Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu and the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (SC-NBWL). Signatories include former Delhi lieutenant governor Najeeb Jung and Prakriti Srivastava, a former principal chief conservator of forests in Kerala.

According to the letter, the project would need 1,416 hectares of forest land, submerge nearly 1,590 hectares and require about 43,000 trees to be felled in an evergreen rainforest. "It (the project) is being pursued since 2011 by different governments, in spite of the havoc it will create on endemic wildlife as well as on tropical rainforests and people," the letter said.

The signatories warned that the dam could threaten the critically endangered white-bellied heron and fragment tiger habitat across the area covering Kamlang, Namdapha and the proposed Dibang Tiger Reserve.

They also traced the approval history. All non-official expert members of the SC-NBWL opposed the project in October 2011, the letter said, but the then Union environment minister granted wildlife clearance in 2012. In 2017 the National Green Tribunal suspended the approvals and directed a fresh examination, including cumulative downstream impacts.

The former officials alleged that a reconstituted wildlife committee cleared the project in 2018 without the multi-seasonal assessment the tribunal had sought, relying on what they called a flawed Wildlife Institute of India study.

The project stalled because of its developer's financial difficulties, among other factors, before the Greenko Group acquired it in 2026. The signatories said the SC-NBWL, reconstituted in March 2026 with only two independent experts, considered the proposal in July mainly to approve the change of developer from Athena to Greenko. They alleged it did not carry out a fresh wildlife assessment and relied on 2018 data.

The letter also disputed the argument that large dams in Arunachal Pradesh would help India establish prior rights over river waters and counter Chinese hydropower upstream on the Brahmaputra. Without a bilateral water-sharing treaty, the signatories argued, downstream infrastructure would not stop China from diverting water.
No response was immediately available from the Union environment ministry or the Arunachal administration, Hindustan Times reported.
keyFacts: 69 former bureaucrats signed a letter dated November 23 against the Demwe Lower project.
The project is a proposed 1,750 MW hydroelectric plant on the Lohit River.
It would divert 1,416 hectares of forest and fell about 43,000 trees, the letter says.
The Greenko Group acquired the project in 2026; the SC-NBWL considered it in July.
stories.background: The project received initial environmental clearance in 2010 and wildlife clearance in 2012. Mishmi and other indigenous communities and environmental groups have opposed it, citing the sacred Parashuram Kund and downstream ecosystems. The National Green Tribunal suspended its approvals in 2017.
stories.whyItMatters: The SC-NBWL and the environment ministry must decide whether the project proceeds, with forest land, wildlife habitat and Mishmi communities in the Lohit valley directly affected.

stories.headline: Xiamen Airlines agrees to buy 50 Boeing 737 jets in $7.4 billion deal
stories.dek: China Southern's subsidiary signed the largest Chinese order for the US planemaker in nearly a decade; deliveries are scheduled from 2031 to 2034, subject to approvals.
stories.summary: China Southern Airlines said its subsidiary Xiamen Airlines agreed on Tuesday to buy 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 jets at a list price of about $7.4 billion. It is Boeing's biggest China order in nearly a decade.
body: China Southern Airlines said in a filing on Tuesday that its subsidiary Xiamen Airlines had agreed to buy 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft at a combined list price of about $7.4 billion, the largest Chinese order for the US planemaker in nearly a decade.

The jets are due to be delivered in batches between 2031 and 2034. The deal is subject to approval from China Southern's shareholders and relevant Chinese government authorities, the filing said. It added that the purchase would be financed through internal funds and external financing.
The actual price will be lower than the list price because of discounts from Boeing, China Southern said. It did not disclose the final figure, citing confidentiality provisions in the agreement.

The company said the order would support Xiamen Airlines' move to the new Xiamen Xiang'an International Airport, help build an aviation hub in Fujian province and improve its fleet structure. China Southern owns 55% of Xiamen Airlines, according to CNBC.

The order follows a commitment for 200 Boeing jets that China made during a summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing in May. Jefferies said in a research note that it understood this was the first conversion of that commitment into a firm order.
The filing did not say whether the order forms part of the 200-jet commitment, and China has not announced specific orders under it. Boeing declined to comment. Its shares rose 1 per cent on Tuesday.
Trump told CNBC on Monday: "By the way, I sold 250 Boeings to China, and I think they're going to do another 250." He gave no details, and Chinese officials have not confirmed further purchases.

Boeing has been largely shut out of new orders from China since 2017 because of trade tensions between Beijing and Washington, though it has continued delivering planes from older orders. In April, China Southern and Xiamen Airlines also agreed to buy 137 Airbus A320neo family aircraft. China Southern said sourcing from different manufacturers would diversify its fleet.

Other Asian carriers, including Philippine Airlines and Malaysia Aviation Group, have also announced Boeing orders this month. Reuters reported that Malaysia Airlines' parent plans to buy 10 Boeing 787 Dreamliners.
keyFacts: Xiamen Airlines agreed to buy 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 jets on Tuesday.
List price is about $7.4 billion; actual price is discounted and undisclosed.
Deliveries are scheduled in batches from 2031 to 2034.
The deal needs shareholder and Chinese government approval.
China committed to 200 Boeing jets during the May Trump-Xi summit.
stories.background: Boeing had been largely shut out of new Chinese orders since 2017 because of US-China trade tensions. Boeing and Airbus forecast China will need around 9,000 new jets by 2045, more than any other region. Xiamen Airlines, long an all-Boeing operator, took its first Airbus A321neo in early 2023.
stories.whyItMatters: The order is the first sign of firm Chinese buying from Boeing after years of limited orders, though it is not confirmed as part of the 200-jet commitment.

stories.headline: NASA pauses Perseverance science and warns Odyssey fuel may last only months
stories.dek: Radio faults on the rover and a failed reaction wheel on the orbiter have left two of NASA's four Mars missions off duty, the agency said.
stories.summary: Two of NASA's four operating Mars missions, the Perseverance rover and the Odyssey orbiter, have suspended science work after separate technical faults. NASA said Perseverance could resume by the end of November, while Odyssey's fuel may last one to two months without a third reaction wheel.
body: Two of NASA's four missions operating at Mars, the Perseverance rover and the Odyssey orbiter, have suspended science operations after separate technical problems in recent weeks, according to NASA statements and reporting by Ars Technica.

Perseverance's trouble is in its communications system. One of its two UHF radios was unresponsive when the rover powered up on October 30, which triggered an automatic switch to the backup radio and put the rover in safe mode. Teams at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California later found the backup was transmitting at about half its expected power, NASA said in a statement last week.
"The team has stopped using both radios until they can evaluate potential causes of the issues and one or both are deemed safe to resume operating," NASA said.

The rover is sending data directly to Earth over its X-band system, which NASA said gives a "significantly lower data rate" than relaying through orbiters. Mission managers paused science "out of an abundance of caution". They plan to restore the backup UHF radio first, then work on the primary. NASA said the team is hopeful the rover could return to science by the end of November.

Odyssey's problem is more serious. One of its four reaction wheels, used to point the spacecraft, stopped spinning in early November. Another failed in 2013, leaving two working wheels. The orbiter needs at least three to stay oriented correctly.

Without three wheels, NASA said, the spacecraft must rely solely on hydrazine thrusters to stay oriented. Engineers estimate the fuel would last one to two months in that case. Before the fault, managers had expected Odyssey to operate through at least the end of 2028 with "extremely low" fuel use, Jeffrey Plaut, the mission's project scientist at JPL, said in a presentation earlier this year.
Ground teams have had some initial success troubleshooting the wheel, though further testing is needed to determine whether it can be recovered.

Odyssey is one of four orbiters NASA uses to relay data between Earth and the Perseverance and Curiosity rovers. The others are NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and the European Space Agency's ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter and Mars Express. NASA lost contact with its MAVEN orbiter last December.

NASA awarded Blue Origin a $700 million contract in September for a dedicated Mars Telecommunications Network orbiter. The work is on hold while the Government Accountability Office considers a protest by Rocket Lab, which lost the bid. The GAO is expected to rule next month.
keyFacts: Perseverance's backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half its expected power, NASA said.
NASA hopes Perseverance can return to science by the end of November.
Odyssey has two working reaction wheels; it needs at least three.
Without a third wheel, Odyssey's hydrazine could last one to two months, NASA estimates.
The GAO is expected to rule next month on Rocket Lab's protest of the $700 million Blue Origin contract.
stories.background: Odyssey reached Mars orbit in 2001 and is the longest-lived Mars mission. Perseverance is in its sixth year at Mars and last month set a record for the farthest distance driven by a vehicle on another planet, passing the 28.06-mile (45.16-kilometre) mark set by Opportunity. NASA lost contact with MAVEN last December after 11 years at Mars; investigators could not identify a specific root cause.
stories.whyItMatters: Orbiters relay data from the Perseverance and Curiosity rovers to Earth, so the loss of Odyssey would reduce NASA's communications capacity at Mars while the replacement orbiter remains on hold.

stories.headline: White House asks Congress for $2 billion extra for NASA's Artemis programme
stories.dek: The request would lift Artemis's annualised funding rate to $9.8 billion and sits on a list of budget exceptions dominated by defence spending.
stories.summary: The White House has asked Congress to allow a higher rate of operations for NASA's Artemis lunar programme, worth $2 billion. The request is part of a list of funding exceptions sent on Monday night as budget talks continue.
body: The White House on Monday night sent Congress a list of budget exceptions that includes $2 billion for NASA's Artemis lunar programme, according to Ars Technica, which reviewed the document.

The list of so-called "funding anomalies" is dominated by Department of Defense appropriations, including the Golden Dome missile defence programme backed by the Trump administration. The Artemis request is among the largest non-defence items. The document describes it as for a "higher rate of operations".

Artemis received about $7.8 billion in fiscal year 2026. The request would be a 25 percent increase. Technically, the administration is seeking to raise the annualised funding rate for Artemis to $9.8 billion, rather than giving NASA an extra $2 billion at once, Ars Technica reported.

Fiscal year 2027 began on October 1, but Congress and the White House have not agreed a budget. The government, including NASA, has been running on a continuing resolution since then. That measure remains in effect until December 11. By that date the two sides must agree a final budget or another continuing resolution, or the government will shut down.

Ars Technica said another continuing resolution appears the most likely outcome given broad disagreement over funding priorities, which would push a budget deal into the new year and to a Democratic-led House and Senate. The anomalies list signals which priorities the administration wants included in such a measure, which the president would have to sign.

The request appears to be a win for NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, who joined the agency 11 months ago, after the White House had assembled its budget request for fiscal 2027. Ars Technica said this is the first time he has worked with the administration on budget priorities.

The outlet also noted that China's lunar ambitions appear as expansive as NASA's, and that China may land astronauts on the Moon before NASA returns. The funding document carried the line: "Without this funding, activities would be delayed."
keyFacts: The White House sent its list of funding anomalies to Congress on Monday night.
The Artemis request is $2 billion for a "higher rate of operations".
Artemis received about $7.8 billion in fiscal year 2026.
The annualised rate would rise to $9.8 billion.
The current continuing resolution runs until December 11.
stories.background: The US government has operated under a continuing resolution since fiscal year 2027 began on October 1, as Congress and the White House have not agreed a budget. Funding anomalies are exceptions to the flat funding such resolutions normally provide.
stories.whyItMatters: If Congress includes the exception in a new continuing resolution, Artemis could operate at a higher rate than flat funding would allow. Without it, the document says, activities would be delayed.

stories.headline: GalaxEye signs deal for Bellatrix propulsion systems on 30 satellites
stories.dek: The multi-year contract is described as the largest order one Indian private space company has placed with another since the sector opened to private players in 2020.
stories.summary: Bengaluru-based Bellatrix Aerospace will supply in-space propulsion systems for the next 30 satellites built by GalaxEye, the companies said on Tuesday. The contract's value was not disclosed.
body: GalaxEye and Bellatrix Aerospace, both based in Bengaluru, signed a multi-year contract on Tuesday under which Bellatrix will supply in-space propulsion systems for the next 30 satellites GalaxEye is building.

A press release described it as the largest business-to-business order one Indian private space company has placed with another since the sector opened to private players in 2020. The financial details were not disclosed.

The agreement was unveiled at the 5th India International Space Conclave in New Delhi, organised by the Indian Space Association. Private companies have taken part in India's space sector from its early years, but usually as suppliers to the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), according to The Hindu.

GalaxEye is building what it calls the world's first OptoSAR satellite constellation. The company says the imaging technology lets customers see any place on Earth through clouds, smoke and darkness. Bellatrix makes electric and green propulsion systems for satellites and orbital transfer vehicles, with hardware already flight-tested on ISRO missions.

"OptoSAR satellites are demanding customers. They need precise, repeatable orbits across a whole constellation, not a single demonstration," said Rohan M. Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of Bellatrix Aerospace, in a statement. He said the company has built production lines to deliver that performance at constellation scale.
Suyash Singh, co-founder and CEO of GalaxEye, said in a statement: "Drishti taught us that every critical system on a satellite has to be one we can see, test and improve up close."

Mission Drishti was launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 on May 3, 2026, and became the first OptoSAR satellite in orbit. GalaxEye said it validated spacecraft deployment, attitude control, onboard computing and in-house mission operations before contact was lost after a geomagnetic storm.

In September, the Technology Development Board of the Department of Science and Technology committed ₹63.84 crore from the government's Research, Development and Innovation Fund for GalaxEye's next multi-sensor satellite. It targets imagery sharper than 0.5 metres.
At the conclave, ISRO chairman V. Narayanan said 440 start-up companies are working in the space area. He said 70-80% of the budget for a launch or satellite goes to Indian industry.

Pawan Goenka, chairman of InSpace, the single-window regulatory and promotional body for the private space sector, said India's priority was now generating demand. "I have less concern about capacity being created; I see a bigger need for demand to be created," he said. He also called for more money in the sector and continued policy stability.
keyFacts: Bellatrix Aerospace will supply propulsion systems for 30 GalaxEye satellites under a multi-year contract signed on November 24.
The contract's financial terms were not disclosed.
Mission Drishti launched on a Falcon 9 on May 3, 2026; contact was lost after a geomagnetic storm.
The Technology Development Board committed ₹63.84 crore in September for GalaxEye's next satellite.
ISRO chairman V. Narayanan said 440 start-ups work in the space area.
stories.background: India opened its space sector to private players in 2020. Private firms have long supplied ISRO, and InSpace now acts as the single-window regulatory and promotional body for private space activity.
stories.whyItMatters: The order shows Indian private space firms buying from each other rather than only supplying ISRO. Officials at the conclave said building demand for such products remains the next task for the sector.

stories.headline: Euclid telescope finds quasar that existed 630 million years after Big Bang
stories.dek: The object, nicknamed Dún Aonghas, hosts a black hole of about 360 million solar masses, according to the researchers who reported it.
stories.summary: Astronomers using the European Space Agency's Euclid telescope have identified what they describe as the most distant quasar known, seen as it was 630 million years after the Big Bang. Its black hole had already grown to about 360 million times the sun's mass.
body: Astronomers have identified the most distant quasar yet observed, a bright galactic core seen as it was 630 million years after the Big Bang, the European Space Agency announced on Tuesday.

The object, formally designated J1504+6252 and nicknamed Dún Aonghas, was first detected by ESA's Euclid telescope. Researchers then characterised it using a combination of ground-based and space-based telescopes. The findings were published in the journal Astronomy and Astrophysics.
The light now reaching Earth left the quasar about 13.1 billion years ago, when the universe was roughly 5% of its present age. The universe is about 13.8 billion years old.

"Just 630 million years after the Big Bang, this black hole had already grown to about 360 million times the mass of the sun and was shining as a quasar," said Julien Wolf of the European Southern Observatory in Germany, the study's lead author. He said the result adds to evidence that some objects in the early universe developed remarkably quickly.

A quasar is the extremely bright core of an active galaxy, powered by gas falling into a supermassive black hole. Silvia Belladitta, a co-author at the Max Planck Institute for Astronomy and the INAF Bologna Observatory of Astrophysics and Space Science, said the infalling material forms a swirling accretion disk that heats to extreme temperatures. She said it can outshine the rest of the galaxy by factors of hundreds or even thousands.

"This makes quasars visible across billions of light-years, allowing us to observe them from the very early universe," Belladitta said. She added that studying them helps astronomers understand how the first galaxies formed and how the black holes at their centres grew so large.
According to the DW report, the discovery supports a scenario in which supermassive black holes form through the direct collapse of large gas clouds and then accumulate more matter.
Euclid is an ESA orbiting telescope designed to investigate dark matter, the invisible material that holds galaxies together, and dark energy, the force that pushes them apart.
keyFacts: The quasar J1504+6252, nicknamed Dún Aonghas, is seen as it was 630 million years after the Big Bang.
Its black hole is about 360 million times the mass of the sun.
Light from the object left it about 13.1 billion years ago.
Euclid first detected it; the study appears in Astronomy and Astrophysics.
Julien Wolf of the European Southern Observatory led the research.
stories.background: Quasars are a brief phase in a galaxy's life, when gas falling into a central supermassive black hole makes the nucleus outshine the rest of the system. Because they are so luminous, they can be seen across billions of light-years, which lets astronomers study the early universe.
stories.whyItMatters: Finding a black hole of this mass so early gives astronomers evidence to test how the first supermassive black holes and galaxies formed and grew.

stories.headline: Rural sites near Delhi record PM2.5 about 20% higher than urban sites, study finds
stories.dek: Researchers from IIT Delhi and UC Berkeley say villages had higher readings than urban areas in every month from July to November 2024, mostly at morning and evening peaks.
stories.summary: A study by IIT Delhi and the University of California, Berkeley found PM2.5 about 20% higher on average at rural sites than urban ones around Delhi. Rural levels were higher in each month of the July to November 2024 monitoring period.
body: Rural areas in and around Delhi recorded PM2.5 concentrations about 20% higher on average than urban areas between July and November 2024, according to a study by researchers from IIT Delhi and the University of California, Berkeley.

The team set up 49 sensor-based monitoring sites along a 160-km transect covering Delhi and the surrounding region. Of these, 32 were rural and 17 urban. Rural readings were higher than urban ones in every one of the five months.

The study, titled 'Rural outdoor air pollution exceeds urban levels in the Delhi megacity region', found the gap was widest in the morning and evening. Rural sites showed sharp peaks between 5am and 8am and again between 5pm and 8pm, while urban sites showed flatter patterns through the day. Levels in the two settings were similar around midday, when the air mixes and disperses pollutants most.

In October and November, the median morning PM2.5 peak was 301 micrograms per cubic metre in rural areas against 252 at urban sites. The median evening peak was 263 against 210. Peak-hour levels were typically 40-50 micrograms per cubic metre higher in villages.

The researchers attributed the rural readings to local combustion, including solid fuels and biomass used for cooking and for preparing fodder. Other sources named were small-scale industries, brick kilns, municipal waste burning and older vehicles.

In urban areas, particularly the capital, the study identified traffic, construction and commercial activity as major local sources. It said domestic biomass burning was less common in more affluent parts of Delhi but continued in some lower-income neighbourhoods.
The urban sites are in south, east, north-west, west and north Delhi, Rohtak and Faridabad. The rural sites are in north-west Delhi, Sonipat, Panipat, Rohtak, Faridabad and Jind.

The authors are Sagnik Dey, Sofiya Rao and Amarendra Singh of IIT Delhi, and Joshua Apte, Mark Joseph Campmier and Maria Teresa Hernandez of Berkeley. Saumya Singh, Nidhi Malik, Swagata Dey, Ajay Pillarisetti and Kalpana Balakrishnan are also listed as authors.
keyFacts: The study used 49 sensor sites: 32 rural and 17 urban, along a 160-km transect.
Monitoring ran from July to November 2024; rural PM2.5 was higher in every month.
October-November median morning peak: 301 micrograms per cubic metre rural, 252 urban.
October-November median evening peak: 263 micrograms per cubic metre rural, 210 urban.
Rural and urban levels were similar around midday.
stories.background: The findings challenge a commonly held perception that cities in India are more polluted than villages, The Times of India reported.
stories.whyItMatters: The readings suggest villagers around Delhi are exposed to fine particulate pollution at levels at or above those in urban areas, particularly in the early morning and evening.

stories.headline: CAS restores Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations champions, overturning CAF ruling
stories.dek: Morocco's football federation said it plans to challenge the verdict in Switzerland's supreme court, alleging contact between a CAS arbitrator and Senegal's federation president.
stories.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport on Tuesday upheld Senegal's appeal and returned the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title, set aside by CAF in March. Morocco, who had been awarded the title, are confirmed runners-up but say they will appeal.
body: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Tuesday upheld an appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) and restored Senegal as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions, overturning a Confederation of African Football (CAF) ruling that had given the title to Morocco.

CAS said its three judges were unanimous. It set aside the decision of the CAF Appeal Board and reinstated the earlier ruling of the CAF Disciplinary Board. "Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed," the court said.

Senegal won the final in Morocco on January 18 by 1-0 after extra time. With the score at 0-0 in second-half stoppage time, Senegal's players walked off in protest when the referee, Jean-Jacques Ndala of Congo, awarded Morocco a penalty. Play resumed after a delay of about 15 minutes. Brahim Diaz's penalty was saved, and Senegal scored in extra time.

In March, a CAF appeals panel ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match by leaving the pitch and awarded Morocco a 3-0 win. Tournament regulations say a team that leaves the ground before the end of a match without the referee's authorisation is considered the loser.

CAS said those rules apply only when a team's conduct leads the referee to call off a game permanently. It said Ndala "did not err in law" in resuming play and had "sole authority" to do so, a decision it said was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.
"The panel acknowledged that the referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension," CAS said. It added that this did not justify calling the decision arbitrary.
Senegalese federation president Abdoulaye Fall said in a statement that CAS "has delivered justice to sport". The FSF posted on social media: "Once again and forever, champions of Africa."

The Royal Moroccan Football Federation said it would appeal, likely to Switzerland's supreme court. Its statement alleged "confirmed communication" between the German arbitrator Ulrich Haas and Fall 48 hours before the decision was issued. The sources do not carry a response from Haas, Fall or CAS to that allegation.
CAS rulings can be challenged at the Swiss court only on limited procedural grounds, which include a judge's integrity. CAS has promised a full written ruling setting out its reasons.
The next men's Africa Cup of Nations begins in June, co-hosted by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.
keyFacts: CAS panel of three judges ruled unanimously for Senegal on Tuesday, November 24.
The final was played on January 18; Senegal won 1-0 after extra time.
CAF's appeals panel had awarded Morocco a 3-0 win in March.
Morocco's federation plans an appeal, alleging contact between arbitrator Ulrich Haas and Abdoulaye Fall.
The next men's AFCON starts in June in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.
stories.background: CAF fined and banned players from both teams about 10 days after the final, with fines of more than $1 million. In March it declared that Senegal had forfeited the match. Senegal's players paraded the trophy before a game against Peru that month, and both teams played at the World Cup believing themselves Africa's rightful champions. CAS held a closed hearing in Lausanne in October.
stories.whyItMatters: The ruling settles, for now, which country holds the continental title, though Morocco's planned challenge to the Swiss supreme court means the dispute may continue.

stories.headline: Sinner has knee surgery, putting Australian Open return in doubt
stories.dek: The Italian, who has not played since winning Wimbledon in July, said conservative treatment failed to settle an iliotibial band problem; no recovery timeline has been announced.
stories.summary: Jannik Sinner said he underwent minor surgery on his iliotibial band on Tuesday after months of unsuccessful non-surgical treatment. He has not played since Wimbledon, and the Australian Open begins on January 17.
body: Jannik Sinner, the two-time Australian Open champion, said on Tuesday he has had minor surgery on his right knee, leaving his planned return at the Melbourne major in January in considerable doubt.

In a statement posted on Instagram, the 25-year-old said the operation was meant to "improve the condition of my iliotibial band". "Over the past few months, together with my team we've tried everything to treat my injury without surgery," he wrote. He said his knee had not responded after some early encouraging progress.
He added: "I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team."

No recovery timeline has been given. The Guardian reported the operation seemed almost certain to rule out an Australian Open comeback, while ABC said his plans had all but been scrapped. BBC Sport noted the tournament is seven weeks away. The Guardian said the surgery was carried out by Finnish orthopaedic specialist Professor Lasse Lempainen.

The iliotibial band is a thick band of connective tissue running along the outside of the leg. The Guardian said injuries to it are typically caused by overuse. Tuesday's post was the first time Sinner had specified the nature of the problem.
Sinner has not played competitively since beating Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final on July 12, his fifth Grand Slam title. He ended his season in early October.

Earlier in November he said his aim was to go to Australia and possibly play a few tournaments before the Grand Slam. He also said he had to respect medical protocols "because if we rush things we could have more serious problems". He said he wants to keep playing for another 10 to 15 years.
In October he said he had lost a lot of weight after having his tonsils removed. He described days when he could play without trouble and others when he could barely move.

Zverev has taken the world No 1 ranking in his absence and finished the year top. Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals on Sunday and is 350 ranking points behind Sinner, according to BBC Sport, though he must defend 2,000 points in Melbourne as reigning champion.
"It's a shame we don't have Jannik," Alcaraz told SuperTennis TV. "I can't wait to see him fit, healthy." The Australian Open main draw begins on January 17.

stories.background: Sinner won the first five Masters 1000 titles of the year and completed the career Golden Masters, but lost early at the French Open, where Zverev won his first Grand Slam title. He then won Wimbledon after a fall in his opening match. Alcaraz returned from a four-month wrist injury layoff in September and won four titles.
stories.whyItMatters: Sinner won in Melbourne in 2024 and 2025, so his absence would remove a two-time champion from the draw and affect the ranking race with Alcaraz and Zverev.

stories.headline: Real Madrid beat PSV 5-1 as City and Arsenal both drop points
stories.dek: Jude Bellingham scored a long-range goal from the bench and Kylian Mbappé added two, while Manchester City drew 2-2 with Napoli and Arsenal 1-1 with Dortmund.
stories.summary: Real Madrid came from 1-0 down to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday, their tenth straight win in all competitions. Manchester City and Arsenal, both at home, failed to win.
body: Real Madrid overturned a first-half deficit to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 at the Santiago Bernabeu on Tuesday, with Jude Bellingham scoring from long range after coming on at half-time and Kylian Mbappé adding two goals.

PSV led through an Ivan Perisic penalty in the 32nd minute. Federico Valverde equalised early in the second half, and Bellingham put Madrid ahead in the 60th minute with a volley off the post after controlling the ball with both feet. Mbappé scored in the 64th and 84th minutes, and Vinícius Júnior added a fifth in the 87th.

The result was Madrid's tenth straight win in all competitions and fifth in the league phase. They have 15 points, three more than Paris Saint-Germain, who host Roma on Wednesday. Mbappé has scored in every Champions League game this season.

At the Etihad Stadium, Manchester City drew 2-2 with Napoli, who had Kevin De Bruyne in their starting line-up. Rasmus Højlund put Napoli ahead in the 55th minute, Ayyoub Bouaddi equalised in the 67th for his first senior goal, and Noa Lang volleyed Napoli back in front in the 76th. Rayan Cherki levelled in the 86th with a low shot inside the near post.

It was the seventh time in 10 games that City had conceded first. Their winless run in the Premier League stands at four matches. Coach Enzo Maresca said: "We take the point." Striker Erling Haaland said: "Not good enough and we let them in too easy." City visit Arsenal on Sunday.

Arsenal drew 1-1 with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates. Viktor Gyökeres scored from outside the area in the 10th minute, and Maximilian Beier equalised in the 55th. Arsenal had 30 shots, and a goal by Jobe Bellingham for Dortmund was ruled out for offside, according to The Guardian.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said: "We want to win every game and today we didn't manage to make that difference in the scoring unfortunately." Arsenal, who played with Kepa Arrizabalaga in goal in place of the injured David Raya, host Real Madrid in two weeks.

Elsewhere, Como beat AEK Athens 1-0 through Luis Milla and have 12 points. Bodø/Glimt beat LASK 1-0 with a stoppage-time own goal, and Galatasaray beat Aston Villa 1-0. Slovan Bratislava lost 2-0 to Real Betis and remain without a point.
keyFacts: Real Madrid beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1; Mbappé scored twice and Bellingham once.
Madrid lead the table with 15 points, three ahead of Paris Saint-Germain.

stories.background: Arsenal were also held on Saturday by Newcastle after leading at half-time. City have not won in the Premier League in four matches. Dortmund lead the Bundesliga by two points from Bayern Munich.
stories.whyItMatters: Madrid's win keeps them top of the league phase, while City and Arsenal, who meet on Sunday, both dropped points.

stories.headline: Namma Metro Blue Line trial runs begin from KR Puram, public opening targeted mid-2027
stories.dek: Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said signalling work and safety certification will take another seven to eight months before the Outer Ring Road stretch opens.
stories.summary: Trial runs have started on the first four stations of Namma Metro's 19-km Blue Line Phase 2A from KR Puram. Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said public operations are targeted for mid-2027, after signalling installation and mandatory certification.
body: Trial runs on Namma Metro's Blue Line began from KR Puram on Tuesday across the first four stations, with public operations on the 19-km Phase 2A corridor targeted for mid-2027, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said.

Gowda inspected the trials at Doddanekkundi station. The train is running from KR Puram to Doddanekkundi. Testing is to extend to another four stations next month, and then progressively to the remaining stations.

Installation of the automatic signalling system is pending. Gowda said it is expected to be completed over the next two to three months, with the government aiming for January. Safety certification would begin after February. "Considering the testing and certification requirements, the entire process is likely to take another seven to eight months before the corridor is opened for public use," he said.

The Times of India reported that the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (BMRCL) must still finish station works at Ibbalur and Silk Board, and complete work at the Byappanahalli depot. It must also obtain an independent safety assessment of the signalling, testing by the Research Designs and Standards Organisation, and authorisation from the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety.

BMRCL has received two trainsets from BEML, enough for the current trials, the paper reported. Space constraints at the depot limit the stabling of more trains, and officials expect this to be resolved by February. BEML is due to supply 66 trainsets in all. BMRCL managing director PC Jaffer said the corporation has not decided whether to open the 19-km stretch in phases or all at once.
The Phase 2A section has 13 stations between KR Puram and Central Silk Board. Gowda said an estimated 11-12 lakh people work along the Outer Ring Road.

The full 58.2-km Blue Line runs from Central Silk Board through KR Puram and Hebbal to Kempegowda International Airport. It is being built at an estimated cost of around ₹20,000 crore, and the government has set a target of completing it within 18 months. Gowda said officials have been told to speed up Phase 2B work with contractors, particularly on the KR Puram-Hebbal stretch.

On finances, Gowda said a rise in the dollar from around ₹70-80 at the time of borrowing to nearly ₹100 had added about 30 per cent to the loan repayment burden. He said the state was releasing funds so that money does not delay projects. BMRCL records an annual loss of ₹600 crore to ₹700 crore including depreciation, he said, and no decision has been taken on raising fares.

On the proposed Red Line, Gowda said the state is still awaiting final approval from the Centre. He said a recent meeting with Central Government officials in Delhi discussed the proposal constructively but reached no decision.
keyFacts: Trials began on Tuesday, November 24, across the first four stations from KR Puram.
Phase 2A is 19 km long with 13 stations, from KR Puram to Central Silk Board.
Signalling installation is targeted for January; certification would begin after February.
The full 58.2-km Blue Line to the airport is estimated to cost around ₹20,000 crore.
BEML is due to supply 66 trainsets; two have been delivered.
stories.background: Gowda said the need for metro connectivity along the Outer Ring Road was identified in 2016-17, when planning for Phases 2A and 2B began. The State Cabinet approved the projects in 2017, proposals went to the Union Government, and construction began in 2020.
stories.whyItMatters: An estimated 11-12 lakh people work along the Outer Ring Road, and they will have to wait roughly seven to eight more months for the Phase 2A line to open to the public.

stories.headline: Karnataka notifies 50% women's quota for zilla and taluk panchayat seats
stories.dek: Rural development minister Eshwar Khandre said elections are expected in January, though the state election commission is yet to receive final electoral rolls.
stories.summary: Karnataka on Tuesday notified reservations for 4,681 zilla and taluk panchayat seats, raising the women's quota from 33% to 50%. Minister Eshwar Khandre said polls are expected in January, subject to final electoral rolls.
body: The Karnataka government on Tuesday notified reservations for 4,681 zilla and taluk panchayat seats, raising the share reserved for women from 33% to 50%, according to The Times of India.

Rural development and panchayati raj minister Eshwar Khandre said the list covers 1,101 zilla panchayat seats and 3,580 taluk panchayat seats. "With this exercise, state govt's role is complete," he said.

Khandre said elections were expected in January. The state election commission, however, has yet to receive the final electoral rolls from the Election Commission, a gap that could hold up the announcement of a poll schedule, the Times of India reported. The state commission must publish draft electoral rolls before it finalises the voters' list.
The government withheld the reservation list for Bengaluru zilla panchayat.

Elections to 30 zilla panchayats and 234 taluk panchayats have not been held since their terms ended in 2021. The last such elections were in 2016, leaving the rural local bodies without elected representatives for nearly five years.
Khandre criticised the previous BJP government, saying it had failed to conduct the elections until 2023. "When Congress took charge, we took up many pending panchayat upgrades," he said.

stories.whyItMatters: The notification is a step towards restoring elected representatives in rural local bodies that have had none for nearly five years, with half the seats reserved for women.
