stories.headline: Indiranagar residents file over 1,200 objections to felling of 137 trees
stories.dek: Most objections were emailed through a webpage shared in RWA WhatsApp groups; the redevelopment of the BDA complex is under challenge in the Karnataka High Court.
stories.summary: The Greater Bengaluru Authority has received more than 1,210 objections to a proposal to clear 137 trees for redevelopment of the BDA complex in Indiranagar, according to GBA data. Nearly 1,200 came by email through a resident-led online initiative.
body: The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has received more than 1,210 objections to a proposal to clear 137 trees for the redevelopment of the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) complex in Indiranagar, according to GBA data.
Nearly 1,200 of the objections arrived by email after a resident welfare association (RWA) initiative encouraged local residents to oppose the clearance, The Hindu reported on Tuesday.

Jaikanth Sekar, an Indiranagar resident and AI engineer, built a webpage that sets out details of the project and the impact of felling trees. The link was shared in RWA WhatsApp groups. Residents who agreed with the concerns could click a "Send Objection" option, which opened an email draft addressed to GBA officials.

According to documents seen by The Hindu, the trees belong to about 22 species, including Mahogany, Indian Fig and Indian Tulip. The largest numbers are African Tulip (32), Silver Oak (23), Rain Tree (22), Peepal (13) and Nile Trumpet (10). Most fall within the proposed construction area.
The contractor's proposal says 38 trees would be retained in situ, 30 transplanted within the project periphery and 69 relocated elsewhere.

All the objections raise a common point: the redevelopment is under challenge before the Karnataka High Court, which has reserved its judgment. The objectors said the court had allowed demolition of the existing structure but, through an interim order, directed that construction should not begin without its permission.

They alleged that removing trees to make way for the project would be a step towards construction and would not be covered by the interim order. They urged the GBA not to consider the application and to revoke the public notice.

A senior GBA official said the notice and the objections must go before the Tree Committee whether trees are to be transplanted or felled. The committee alone decides how the trees will be dealt with, the official said.
The official added that even after the committee submits its report, permission for clearance will be granted or denied only after the High Court delivers its order.
keyFacts: GBA has received over 1,210 objections to clearing 137 trees in Indiranagar.
Nearly 1,200 objections were sent by email via a webpage built by resident Jaikanth Sekar.
Contractor proposes retaining 38 trees, transplanting 30 and relocating 69.
The Karnataka High Court has reserved judgment on the BDA complex redevelopment.
stories.background: The project involves redevelopment of the BDA Shopping Complex in Indiranagar. The High Court allowed demolition of the existing structure but, by interim order, barred construction without its permission. The GBA recently received around 1,600 objections to tree-felling for the Hebbal Short Tunnel, The Hindu noted.
stories.whyItMatters: The Tree Committee must consider the objections, and the GBA official said no clearance permission will be decided until the High Court rules.

stories.headline: Chennai Corporation floats ₹30.06-crore tender for pedestrian works in five neighbourhoods
stories.dek: The seven-package project covers 16.26 km in Adyar, Besant Nagar, Thiruvanmiyur, Royapettah and Triplicane, while residents elsewhere report footpaths blocked by vendors, parked vehicles and ramps.
stories.summary: The Greater Chennai Corporation has floated tenders worth ₹30.06 crore for pedestrian infrastructure across parts of south and central Chennai. Residents of several neighbourhoods say footpath encroachment persists across the city.
body: The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has floated tenders worth ₹30.06 crore to improve pedestrian infrastructure in parts of Adyar, Besant Nagar, Thiruvanmiyur, Royapettah and Triplicane, The Times of India reported.

The work is divided into seven packages with a combined proposed development length of 16.26 km. It falls under Phase 1 of the Integrated Non-Motorised Transport Neighbourhood Development programme, part of the Chennai Metropolitan Infrastructure Development and Urban Management Scheme.

A GCC source said the works include footpaths with a minimum clear width of 1.8 m, tactile paving for visually impaired pedestrians, ramps and bollards. They also cover smart streets with better lighting, landscaping, street furniture, pedestrian plazas and organised parking, and junction redesigns for safer crossings.

In Adyar, Sardar Patel Road is to be developed as a smart street. A Safe School Access Network is planned around 42 identified schools, with safer crossings, traffic-calming measures and designated pick-up and drop-off zones. Footpaths are to be improved in Kottur Gardens, Besant Nagar, Indira Nagar and Kasthuribai Nagar.

In Royapettah and Triplicane, the plans include redevelopment of Wallajah Road as a smart street, footpath upgrades near Chepauk railway station and along Bharathi Salai, and junction improvements. The area has 43 identified schools.

S Saravanan, deputy commissioner (works) at GCC, said: "The integrated approach would improve pedestrian safety and accessibility while making neighbourhood streets more convenient for all road users."

Separately, The Hindu reported that residents in Vyasarpadi, Abhiramapuram, Anna Nagar, Aminjikarai, T. Nagar, Velachery and Mylapore frequently complain of shrinking pedestrian space, with some forced to walk on roads. Obstructions listed include roadside shops, parked vehicles, cafe seating, utilities and ramps from private properties.

GCC recently removed illegal roadside shops in Ashok Nagar and Anna Nagar, and residents have asked for similar drives citywide and for regular monitoring to stop vendors returning. Sandhya Vedullapalli of the Federation of Anna Nagar Residents Associations said the Town Vending Committee "must take a more proactive role in regulating street vending".

The Wallace Garden and Rutland Gate Residents' Association said Khader Nawaz Khan Road in Teynampet, redesigned for pedestrians, faces fresh problems including roadside parking and pavement occupation. According to GCC Budget documents, the budget estimate for pavement operation and maintenance in 2026-27 is ₹66,601, against ₹51,229 spent in 2024-25.

Proposed combined development length is 16.26 km.
Footpaths are to have a minimum clear width of 1.8 m.

Khader Nawaz Khan Road in Teynampet received the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry's Award of Excellence for the city with the Best Non-Motorised Transport System, according to a residents' association note.

stories.headline: Transport union protests at MTC headquarters over private e-bus operations
stories.dek: The Government Transport Workers Union wants the state to run all 625 electric buses directly and to regularise contract staff who have completed three years of service.
stories.summary: Members of the Government Transport Workers Union and families of employees protested outside the MTC headquarters in Chennai on Tuesday against private operation of electric buses. Police detained the protesters and released them in the evening.
body: Members of the Government Transport Workers Union staged a protest in front of the Metropolitan Transport Corporation (MTC) headquarters in Chennai on Tuesday, demanding that the state government take over the operation of electric buses and end private participation.
The North Chennai, Central Chennai and South Chennai district committees organised the protest jointly with the union. Family members of transport employees also took part.
The union said nearly 45 lakh passengers use MTC buses every day. It alleged that outsourcing electric bus operations to private operators amounted to privatisation of public transportation.

The union also alleged that the previous DMK government had handed over MTC routes to a private firm in 2025 for operating 625 electric buses. Claiming large-scale irregularities in the arrangement, the protesters demanded an inquiry.

V Dayanandam, the union's general secretary, spoke about the position of contract workers. "Despite working as hard as the permanent employees, the contract workers are not eligible for several benefits. Moreover, the employees have lost social security. Reservation is not followed while appointing employees by private firms," he said.

The protesters demanded a government takeover of all 625 electric buses and direct operation by the MTC. They also sought permanent absorption of staff and regularisation of contract workers who have completed three years of service.
Police detained the protesters for disrupting traffic and released them in the evening.

stories.headline: Three held, two of them women, after cafe worker alleges gang rape in Preet Vihar
stories.dek: Delhi Police are searching for three other accused after the 22-year-old woman, a colleague of all six, approached them on Tuesday morning.
stories.summary: Delhi Police arrested three people, including two women, after a 22-year-old cafe worker alleged she was gang-raped by two male colleagues at a Preet Vihar cafe early on Tuesday. Three other accused are absconding.
body: Delhi Police have arrested three people, including two women, after a 22-year-old woman alleged that two male colleagues gang-raped her at a cafe in Preet Vihar, east Delhi, in the early hours of Tuesday.

Three other accused are absconding and efforts are under way to trace them, Deputy Commissioner of Police (East) Rajeev Kumar said. An FIR has been registered against six people, four men and two women, according to News18.
Mr. Kumar said the woman and the six accused worked as attendants and waiters at a cafe in a mall near Karkardooma Court. All are Delhi residents.

After the workplace closed on Monday night, the group drank alcohol and then went to a colleague's home in Mandawali, where they allegedly drank more, the officer said. At around 2.30 a.m. they went to Saltanate Cafe in Preet Vihar, which had closed at about 11.30 p.m.

Police said one of the men had earlier worked at the cafe and knew where the keys were kept. According to Mr. Kumar, he called the caretaker to confirm the location, and the group let themselves in and continued drinking.
Around 3.30 a.m., the three women left with a male friend of the victim who had come to pick her up, Mr. Kumar said. The men went to their homes, as CCTV footage checked by police showed.
The Times of India and News18 quoted police as saying eight people had been at the cafe. The Hindu's account counts the victim and six accused, and the sources do not reconcile the figures.

At about 6 a.m., the woman went to the police with her male friend, The Hindu reported. News18 put the time at about 5.45 a.m. She alleged that two male colleagues sexually assaulted her and that the others helped them.
A case has been registered under provisions relating to gang rape. Police said the investigation is continuing.

stories.headline: Delhi SIR claims and objections phase ends Wednesday; final roll due December 22
stories.dek: Electors left out of the draft roll can still submit reprinted enumeration forms until November 30, though Form 6, 7 and 8 applications received after Wednesday will not count for the final roll.
stories.summary: Wednesday is the last day to file claims and objections in the Special Intensive Revision of Delhi's electoral roll. The final roll will be published on December 22, officials said.
body: Wednesday, November 25, is the last day to file claims and objections in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of Delhi's electoral roll, with the final roll scheduled for publication on December 22, election officials said.

The office of the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer, Ashok Kumar, said it had received 3.28 lakh Form 6 applications, 35,155 Form 7 applications and 1.23 lakh Form 8 applications till Tuesday. Form 6 seeks inclusion of a name, Form 7 seeks deletion and Form 8 seeks corrections or a change of residence. The Times of India reported that another 610 Form 6A applications had come from overseas electors.

Applications for addition, deletion or modification received after November 25 will not be considered for the final roll, officials told The Hindu. An official told The Times of India that no further extension of the claims period was likely because the revision has to be completed within the revised schedule.

Separately, electors excluded from the draft roll under the absent, shifted, dead or duplicate (ASDD) categories have until November 30 to submit reprinted enumeration forms with supporting documents. The Election Commission opened this route on November 6 on the directions of the Supreme Court. It covers electors who were issued forms earlier but did not return them. Reprinted forms became available in Delhi on November 19. They can be collected from Booth Level Officers or downloaded from the Election Commission website. Those who have already filed Form 6 need not submit one again.
These cases will be considered with other applications as part of the disposal process, which ends on December 15.

The Times of India gave district figures. West recorded the most Form 6 applications at 39,792, and New Delhi the fewest at 5,741. South East received the most Form 7 applications at 4,808. North East topped Form 8 with 16,729.

The Hindu reported that the CEO's office does not publish a daily count of reprinted forms distributed or returned, so it is unclear how far the second route is reaching excluded electors. Several Electoral Registration Officers described the response as negligible. One officer in the North East district said booth-level staff had not found any excluded electors seeking re-inclusion. Another said fewer than 10 people had asked for the form, all of whom had moved to a different constituency.

The draft contained around 97.5 lakh names. The original claims deadline of October 30 was extended to November 25. That moved the disposal deadline from November 30 to December 15 and final publication from December 4 to December 22.

stories.headline: Man stabs nine police officers in Delhi; police probe gang links
stories.dek: CCTV footage shows personnel running for cover inside Jama Masjid police station as the accused, Nabeel, moved through it, and police are examining whether the officers' preparedness was adequate.
stories.summary: A 30-year-old man wounded nine Delhi Police personnel on Monday, five inside Jama Masjid police station and four in Chitli Qabar, before being shot in the legs and caught. Police are probing possible gang links and whether the response was avoidable.
body: A 30-year-old man identified by police as Mohd Nabeel wounded nine police personnel on Monday, five inside Jama Masjid police station in Delhi and four during his arrest in Chitli Qabar, where police shot him six times.

CCTV footage seen by Hindustan Times and described by The Hindu shows Nabeel entering through the open main gate around 2:30 pm. He walked to the duty officer's desk, where a woman officer and Sub-Inspector Aravind were sitting, and asked who had called him, according to The Hindu. When the woman identified herself, he attacked Aravind's neck and face with a knife.

As panic spread, at least three personnel ran for cover. Nabeel tried to force his way into a room, but the door was shut. Near the lock-up, officers who tried to arm themselves with sticks were attacked, and two were stabbed. One of them, head-constable Harender, was hurt on the face, neck and chest.

An older officer tried to shut the main door, which The Hindu described as a fragile structure of glass and a thin panel. Nabeel pushed through and the officer fell. Another officer who followed with a stick was also stabbed. The footage shows Nabeel walking out past the armed sentry, a woman officer, who could not stop him.

He snatched a two-wheeler at knifepoint. Police teams from several stations tracked him and cornered him in narrow lanes between 4:15 pm and 4:30 pm. Police said he injured four more personnel there, and they fired eight rounds, six of which hit his legs.

Police said Nabeel was called to the station after his mother and sister complained about his aggressive behaviour. Both were in the room when the attack began and ducked under a desk. A senior officer said nobody at the station knew who he was until a wounded officer later explained why two women had come.

DCP (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said three of the injured, SI Ajay, SI Aravind and HC Harender, suffered 2-3-inch-deep wounds and will need surgery. "We are also looking into whether this was avoidable. One major issue was that only a few people were inside because most of the staff was busy with VIP movements in the city," he said.

The Hindu reported that investigators are examining possible links to an organised gang and whether anyone instigated him. They have found no social media accounts of his, police sources said, and are checking whether he had drug use or read religious material. A joint interrogation involving the Intelligence Bureau and other agencies is likely once he regains consciousness.

The Times of India quoted police officers suggesting tasers, stronger sentry duty and stricter entry checks. Another officer said police stations receive people in distress, making the same level of security hard to maintain.

Three FIRs have been registered against Nabeel for attempted murder and robbery. A court has sent him to judicial custody, to be lodged in custody after treatment. All nine injured personnel are out of danger, police said.

stories.headline: Musi rejuvenation Phase-1 work to begin in January 2027, officials tell CM
stories.dek: Officials briefed Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Tuesday that tendering for the first phase has started, and detailed two zones covering about 21 km.
stories.summary: Work on Phase 1 of the Musi rejuvenation project will begin in January 2027, municipal officials told Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Tuesday. The tender process has started, and the review also covered the PRTS, Mir Alam Tank and other projects.
body: Work on Phase 1 of the Musi rejuvenation project in Hyderabad will begin in January 2027, municipal administration and urban development officials told Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy at a review meeting on Tuesday.
The officials said the tender process for Phase 1 has already been initiated and arrangements are under way to start work early next year, according to The Times of India.
Under Phase 1, the 9.20-km stretch from Himayatsagar to Gandhi Sarovar has been designated 'Zone-1 A'. The 11.8-km stretch from Osmansagar to Gandhi Sarovar is 'Zone-1 B'.

The meeting also covered the Personal Rapid Transit System (PRTS). Officials explained the techno-economic feasibility of its Phase 1, including alignment options from Kukatpally through Raidurg to Biodiversity Junction. They also presented proposals running from Begumpet Metro Station through Secretariat, Basheerbagh and Ranigunj.

Reddy asked officials to identify suitable locations for PRTS depots around Necklace Road, Raidurg and People's Plaza and to study their feasibility. "Plans should be developed to include multi-level parking facilities in the vicinity of these depots," he said.

On the Mir Alam Tank project, officials said they were working to finish it by January 2028. The chief minister directed them to remove accumulated silt from the tank as well as carry out its overall development.

Reddy told officials to speed up all projects in the CURE and PURE areas, within and outside the Outer Ring Road, that fall under the municipal department. He also asked for faster construction of the integrated fruit market at Koheda, without compromising on quality, and for road work to be completed alongside it.

HYDRA commissioner AV Ranganath briefed him on lake restoration and protection of government assets, and presented proposals for sewage treatment plants at necessary locations. The chief minister asked for the plants to be built quickly and for stepwells across the city to be restored.

Officials also reported on radial road construction and land acquisition, and Reddy directed them to accelerate the work. He asked that the modern goshala under construction at Gandipet be completed by March 2027.
keyFacts: Musi Phase 1 work is to start in January 2027; tendering has begun.
Zone-1 A runs 9.20 km from Himayatsagar to Gandhi Sarovar.
Zone-1 B runs 11.8 km from Osmansagar to Gandhi Sarovar.
Mir Alam Tank project is targeted for completion by January 2028.
Gandipet goshala is to be completed by March 2027.

stories.headline: Telangana loses ₹50 crore to 'digital arrest' scams in 10 months of 2026
stories.dek: Monthly complaints have fallen to an average of 85, but the Telangana Cyber Security Bureau says gangs still target victims through prolonged video calls.
stories.summary: People in Telangana lost ₹50 crore to 'digital arrest' scams between January and October, the state cyber bureau said. Complaints are falling, but a retired LIC employee in Hyderabad reported losing ₹33.4 lakh this year.
body: People in Telangana lost ₹50 crore to 'digital arrest' scams in the first 10 months of 2026, according to the Telangana Cyber Security Bureau (TGCSB), even as the average number of monthly complaints fell to 85.
The bureau received 846 complaints between January and October, and police registered 241 FIRs. Monthly complaints averaged 101 in 2025 and 253 in 2024.

Since January 2024, the state has recorded 5,097 complaints involving losses of ₹320 crore, with 1,697 FIRs registered. Average monthly losses were ₹5 crore in the first 10 months of 2026, against ₹7.7 crore in 2025 and ₹14.7 crore in 2024.
The average loss per complaint was ₹5.9 lakh this year, compared with ₹7.6 lakh in 2025 and ₹5.8 lakh in 2024, the bureau said.

In one recent case, a 65-year-old retired LIC employee from Masab Tank lost ₹33.40 lakh after being kept under a purported digital arrest for over a month, according to her complaint to Hyderabad Cybercrime police.

She said she received a call in August from a person claiming to be a Karnataka Police constable, who told her she was involved in a money laundering case. A person posing as an IPS officer then contacted her on a WhatsApp video call.

The callers told her she was under digital arrest and must not leave her home without permission from investigating officers, she said. They threatened her with arrest if she left the house, contacted anyone or disobeyed them. She said she complied out of fear.

She was then told to transfer money in the name of the Reserve Bank of India, and sent ₹33.40 lakh in multiple transactions. After realising she had been cheated, she approached the Cybercrime police. A case has been registered and an investigation is under way.

The bureau said fraudsters pose as police, CBI and Enforcement Directorate officers, using forged identity cards and fake arrest warrants. Some calls begin with claims that a parcel in the victim's name contains drugs or forged passports, a tactic documented by the Union home ministry.
"Victims are psychologically threatened and kept under continuous surveillance through video calls, sometimes for several days," the TGCSB said in its submission on digital arrest cases.

The bureau said the gangs operate across states and countries, with members handling calls, bank accounts, fund transfers and cash withdrawals. Callers also impersonate judicial authorities and Telecom Regulatory Authority of India officials.
keyFacts: Telangana lost ₹50 crore to digital arrest scams between January and October 2026.
The TGCSB received 846 complaints in that period; police registered 241 FIRs.
Since January 2024, the state has logged 5,097 complaints and ₹320 crore in losses.
A 65-year-old retired LIC employee from Masab Tank lost ₹33.40 lakh.
stories.background: In digital arrest scams, callers pose as law enforcement or other officials and tell victims they face criminal charges. They keep victims on video calls and press them to move money to accounts the gangs control, saying it must be verified or kept safe.
stories.whyItMatters: Complaint numbers and monthly losses have fallen since 2024, but the average loss per complaint rose in 2025 and remains ₹5.9 lakh this year, so individual victims can still lose large sums.

stories.headline: Illegal groundwater extraction found at multiple sites across Cyberabad, TOI report says
stories.dek: HYDRAA says it will notify areas of sharply depleted groundwater as 'water pressure zones' where extraction will be banned and facilities sealed.
stories.summary: A Times of India ground visit on Tuesday found operators extracting groundwater for tanker sales at several Cyberabad locations, including near lakes and in residential areas. HYDRAA's commissioner said areas with severe depletion will be notified as zones where extraction is prohibited.
body: The Times of India reported that it found multiple operators extracting groundwater for commercial sale across the Cyberabad region of Hyderabad during a visit on Tuesday, including sites at Tellapur, Osman Nagar, Vattinagulapally and near Thammidikunta Lake in Hi-Tec City.

At several locations, groundwater was drawn with high-powered motors, stored in underground sumps and pumped into private tankers parked at the sites, the newspaper said. Some sites were near lakes, in agricultural fields or inside residential neighbourhoods.

Under the Telangana WALTA Act, 2002, extraction of groundwater for commercial sale is prohibited in over-exploited areas, residential localities and recharge zones where it depletes public or private water sources and affects domestic supply. TOI said most of the operators it found were in residential areas or within lake buffer zones.

Near Thammidikunta Lake on Hitex Road, which the report said was recently inaugurated by Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, several tankers were moving in and out continuously. In Vattinagulapally, water was drawn near agricultural fields and channelled into a sump, and at another site behind a petrol pump on the main road, tankers were being filled from a makeshift shelter housing the equipment.

In Tellapur, TOI identified at least four extraction points. Some operators had converted tent house shops into extraction facilities, while others built huts around pipelines and motors. Osmannagar had extraction points with pipelines, motors and electricity meters along roadsides.

Some extraction points had 20 to 30 CCTV cameras to watch their premises and surroundings, the report said. Tankers that TOI followed headed to commercial and residential areas in Gachibowli and Hi-Tec City.

Residents alleged the extraction was lowering the groundwater table and said much of it happened late at night. E Ramana, president of the Tellapur Neighbourhood Association, said residents of the Divine Space community staged a protest asking operators to stop, alleging extraction continued despite recent enforcement operations.

Dr Sai Ravi Shanker, president of the Federation of Gated Communities Cyberabad, questioned the quality of tanker water. He said operators often claim it is treated river water, but that nearly 80% of samples tested by third-party agencies, from tankers costing around Rs 4,000, turned out to be borewell water.

HYDRAA officials said certain exemptions had been extended because hostels, hotels and commercial establishments depend on private tankers. Commissioner AV Ranganath said the agency had asked the groundwater department to identify localities where levels have fallen sharply, and would notify them as 'water pressure zones' where extraction is completely prohibited.
"Extraction points found operating in these notified areas would face immediate enforcement action, including sealing of facilities," Ranganath said.
keyFacts: TOI visited Cyberabad sites on Tuesday and found multiple commercial extraction operations.
At least four extraction points were identified in Tellapur.
Some sites had 20 to 30 CCTV cameras each, TOI reported.
A residents' federation says nearly 80% of tested tanker samples were borewell water.
HYDRAA plans to notify 'water pressure zones' where extraction will be banned.
stories.background: The Telangana WALTA Act, 2002, bars commercial groundwater extraction in over-exploited areas, residential localities and recharge zones. HYDRAA, the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency, says it has extended some exemptions because commercial establishments rely on tankers.
stories.whyItMatters: Residents in Tellapur and nearby areas say falling borewell levels are affecting them, while hotels, hostels and businesses depend on tanker supply.

stories.headline: Kochi Corporation to restrict biomedical waste subsidy from New Year as pickups lag
stories.dek: Households say collection requests on the My Kochi app take nearly three weeks to be met, against a promised four to five days.
stories.summary: From the New Year, Kochi Corporation will limit its biomedical waste subsidy to the extremely poor, persons with disabilities and bedridden and palliative-care patients. Residents report waits of nearly three weeks for pickups, and the LDF opposes the change.
body: Kochi Corporation will limit its doorstep biomedical waste collection subsidy to selected categories of households from the New Year, ending the universal subsidy, The Hindu reported on Tuesday.

Eligible groups are the extremely poor, persons with disabilities, and bedridden and palliative-care patients. Division councillors have received a pro forma for applications, which must carry certificates from the councillor concerned and from medical professionals.
Subsidised collection will cost ₹12 plus GST per kg. Other households will pay ₹20 plus GST, up from the current ₹12. The corporation's own burden will fall to ₹8 per kg.

Mayor V.K. Minimol said some households had disposed of more than 100 kilograms of biomedical waste, which she called unacceptable. Subsidised collection will therefore be capped at 20 kg at a time, she said.

Collection is currently handled by Success Projects, a subsidiary of Raidco Kerala Limited, which runs two biomedical waste incinerators at Brahmapuram. Residents book pickups through the My Kochi app, which lists a wait of four to five days.

The New Indian Express reported that actual waits run close to three weeks. Shameera, 40, of Pachalam, said she waited nearly that long and that one bag of used adult diapers became two and three. Rajeev, a resident of Ponekkara, said staff sometimes did not turn up or asked residents to take waste to another location.

LDF councillor Jagadambika alleged that the contractor's sanitation staff behaved rudely when waste exceeded 26 kg. BJP councillor Sudha Dileepkumar said the company was a 'success' only in name, and Ravipuram councillor S. Sasikala said it often missed designated collection days.

Sources associated with Success Projects told The Hindu the firm collects around 3,000 kg a day on average and that heavy bookings had created a backlog now being cleared. The New Indian Express reported that a broken burner at an incinerator at the treatment plant had caused collected waste to pile up. That report attributed the detail to reports rather than an official statement.
The mayor has directed the contractor to speed up collection.

V.A. Sreejith, the LDF parliamentary party leader, said the front had registered written dissent before the council approved the new system. 'Our position is that the universally subsidised system should continue,' he said. He also said Success Projects was brought in without due process, a claim the sources do not answer.
keyFacts: Subsidised biomedical waste collection will cost ₹12 plus GST per kg; others will pay ₹20 plus GST.
Subsidised pickups will be capped at 20 kg at a time, Mayor V.K. Minimol said.
The My Kochi app promises collection in four to five days; residents report nearly three weeks.
Success Projects says it collects around 3,000 kg of biomedical waste a day.
The LDF opposes ending the universal subsidy.
stories.background: Biomedical waste in Kochi, including items such as used adult diapers, is collected from homes by Success Projects, a subsidiary of Raidco Kerala Limited. Residents register requests on the My Kochi app. The UDF-led council approved the new targeted system after recording the LDF's written dissent.
stories.whyItMatters: Households that do not qualify for the subsidy will pay ₹20 plus GST per kg instead of ₹12, while many already report long waits for collection.

stories.headline: Kalady Sanskrit university appeals order quashing suspension of 16 students
stories.dek: The university told a division bench that the suspension was an interim measure and that the students should have used the grievance redressal route under UGC regulations.
stories.summary: Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady, has appealed to a division bench of the Kerala High Court against a single judge's order quashing the suspension of 16 students. The order also directed special examinations for those who missed them.
body: The Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (SSUS), Kalady, has filed an appeal before a division bench of the Kerala High Court against a single judge's order that quashed the suspension of 16 students, The New Indian Express reported.
Vice-chancellor Ciza Thomas, the university and its syndicate filed the writ appeal on Monday. They seek to set aside the November 23 judgment of Justice P V Kunhikrishnan and to stay its operation.

The single judge had quashed the suspension orders, the constitution of the inquiry committee, its report and the syndicate decision that followed. The report had found the students, who are affiliated with the Students' Federation of India (SFI), guilty of misconduct. The court directed the university to let them attend regular classes and to hold special examinations within six weeks for those who missed their exams. It referred to an undertaking the university had given before the Supreme Court.
The students were accused of staging a mock funeral of Ms Thomas and assaulting her. They denied the allegations and said they were protesting against a lack of infrastructure at the university.

In its appeal, the university said a suspension pending inquiry is an interim measure, not a punishment, meant to preserve the institution's atmosphere during the inquiry. It said the alleged deficiencies in facilities were not recent and that the authorities had always been open to dialogue.
The university said it opposed violence, not dissent. It claimed the vice-chancellor and syndicate members were confined for nearly two hours, a mock funeral was staged and they were assaulted.

The university argued that the students should have approached the Students' Grievance Redressal Committee, with a further appeal to the Ombudsperson under the UGC Regulations, 2023. It said the single judge's finding that this route was not an effective remedy would nullify the regulations.

It also contended that the judge applied the strict rules of departmental or service inquiries to a student disciplinary proceeding, which it said serves a different purpose. The university denied that the inquiry committee violated the principles of natural justice.

On the examinations, the university said the students lacked the required attendance and internal marks. It said its statement before the Supreme Court was conditional and did not override university regulations. The dispute had reached the Supreme Court before it was referred to the single judge.
The appeal asks the division bench to set aside the single judge's order.
keyFacts: The university filed the writ appeal on Monday before a Kerala High Court division bench.
Justice P V Kunhikrishnan's judgment of November 23 quashed the suspension of 16 students.
The single judge ordered special examinations within six weeks for students who missed exams.
The students are affiliated with the SFI and deny assaulting Vice-Chancellor Ciza Thomas.
stories.background: The 16 students were suspended after a protest at the university in which, the university alleges, the vice-chancellor and syndicate members were confined, a mock funeral was staged and the vice-chancellor was assaulted. The students say they were protesting against inadequate infrastructure. The dispute reached the Supreme Court before it was referred to the single judge.
stories.whyItMatters: The division bench's decision will determine whether the 16 students can attend classes and sit special examinations while the case continues.

stories.headline: Cooch Behar infant denied birth certificate after father's name dropped from rolls in SIR
stories.dek: Abdul Habib says officials refused residence verification for his daughter, born on September 9, because he was deleted from the electoral roll; his tribunal appeal is pending.
stories.summary: A two-and-a-half-month-old girl in West Bengal's Cooch Behar has not received a birth certificate after her father's name was deleted in the special intensive revision of electoral rolls. The father says officials called him a Bangladeshi national, which he denies.
body: A two-and-a-half-month-old girl in Cooch Behar district, West Bengal, has been unable to obtain a birth certificate because her father's name was deleted from the electoral rolls during the special intensive revision (SIR), according to a report by The Hindu.

Amina Khatun, a resident of Khatamari village, gave birth to the girl at Dinhata Sub-Divisional Hospital on September 9. She and her husband, Abdul Habib, then approached the hospital and the Panchayat office for the certificate. They were reportedly told to arrange residential verification from the Panchayat Pradhan or the local MLA.

Mr. Habib said he asked Ajoy Roy, the MLA for Dinhata, for the verification, but the MLA's office refused. He was told the certificate could not be issued because his name had been deleted in the SIR.

"An official from the MLA office said that I am a Bangladeshi national and therefore I would need to get myself first registered through the National Register of Citizens," Mr. Habib said. "I have been living in India since my birth. My house in Khatamari was built by my grandfather. I have shown them all the documents, but they still refused." He said the Block Development Officer of Sahebganj turned down a similar request on the same grounds.

Three of Mr. Habib's sisters were also deleted from the rolls. The Election Commission of India called them for a hearing, citing a "logical discrepancy": six other people had also claimed his father as their own. The names of his parents, his wife and his elder sister remain on the voters' list.
Mr. Habib has appealed to a tribunal to have his name restored. The application is awaiting a decision.

The Association for Protection of Civil Rights (APCR) objected to the alleged obstruction. In a statement it said birth registration is a statutory obligation and that "the child's right to legal identity must not be linked to the electoral status of her parents." It asked the government to issue the certificate immediately.
The Hindu said it had not carried responses from the MLA's office or the BDO. The SIR ahead of the Assembly elections removed 91 lakh names from West Bengal's rolls.

In June, Umme Salma of Cooch Behar approached the Calcutta High Court after a ration dealer said her entitlement could stop unless she showed proof of an appeal over her deleted name. The court directed that the state government take no coercive steps on her monthly ration without its permission.
keyFacts: The girl was born on September 9 at Dinhata Sub-Divisional Hospital in Cooch Behar.
Father Abdul Habib's name was deleted from the rolls in the SIR; his tribunal appeal is pending.
Three of his sisters were also deleted over an alleged 'logical discrepancy' involving his father.
The SIR removed 91 lakh names from West Bengal's electoral rolls.
stories.background: The special intensive revision of electoral rolls was held in West Bengal before the Assembly elections. According to The Hindu, residents have in recent months reported being denied basic services or scheme benefits after deletions. In June, the Calcutta High Court shielded a Cooch Behar woman's ration entitlement from coercive action.
stories.whyItMatters: The case shows how deletion from the electoral roll can affect access to documents such as a newborn's birth certificate, which the family says remains unissued.

stories.headline: Bengal moves to adopt 1999 central law repealing urban land ceiling caps
stories.dek: Sources say the state's legal team has vetted the proposal, which needs an assembly resolution and the Centre's approval; a separate bill to replace minor penalties with fines is also planned.
stories.summary: The West Bengal government plans to adopt the central Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Repeal Act, 1999, which would end the 1976 law's caps on urban land holdings, according to sources. A separate Jan Vishwas bill is due in the winter session from December 4-14.
body: The West Bengal government plans to adopt the central Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Repeal Act, 1999, which would end the 50-year-old caps on urban land ownership, The Times of India reported on Wednesday, citing sources.

The state's legal team has already vetted the move, the sources said. A proposal will soon be placed before the assembly, seeking cabinet approval for adoption of the 1999 Act under Article 252(2) of the Constitution, and for the consequential repeal of the 1976 Act as it applies in Bengal.
Both laws are central statutes, so experts said the Centre's approval would be needed after an assembly resolution. Sources said most states have already adopted the 1999 law with central approval.

The 1976 Act set ceilings on vacant urban land: 500 square metres, or seven cottahs, in the Kolkata urban agglomeration, and 2,000 square metres, or 28 cottahs, in the Asansol and Durgapur agglomerations. The Kolkata agglomeration covers the Kolkata Municipal Area and a large part of the Kolkata Metropolitan Area, including Howrah, Hooghly, Serampore and Chandernagore, with some parts of New Town added later.

The law was enacted to prevent urban land from concentrating in a few hands and to allow more equitable distribution. Over the years it has led to difficulties in urban land development and delays in housing and infrastructure projects, the report said.
Sources said repeal may also help residential projects, including affordable housing, "subject to applicable planning, land use and building regulations".

Separately, the state plans to table the West Bengal Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026 during the assembly's winter session from December 4-14, after cabinet clearance. Officials said it would replace jail terms and criminal cases for minor, technical or paperwork lapses with monetary fines.

Bengal would join at least seven states and Union Territories, including Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Haryana, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Delhi, that have passed parallel laws. Officials said the bill would amend statutes including the West Bengal Shops and Establishments Act, 1963, and the Kolkata Municipal Corporation Act, 1980.
A senior official said moving such disputes from magistrate courts to designated departmental officers would reduce judicial backlog, limit arbitrary inspections and ease doing business in the state.
keyFacts: The ceiling is seven cottahs in Kolkata and surrounding areas, and 28 cottahs in some other urban bodies.
The state's legal team has vetted the repeal proposal, according to sources.
Adopting the 1999 Act needs an assembly resolution and central approval, experts said.
The Jan Vishwas bill is due in the assembly's December 4-14 winter session.
stories.background: The Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act was enacted in 1976 to prevent concentration of urban land. The Centre passed a repeal Act in 1999, which states must adopt individually. The central Jan Vishwas Act of 2023 decriminalised 183 provisions across 42 laws; a 2026 amendment followed.
stories.whyItMatters: Repeal would lift ownership caps on vacant urban land in Kolkata, Asansol and Durgapur agglomerations. The Jan Vishwas bill would mean traders face fines rather than prosecution for minor lapses.

stories.headline: Rebel Trinamool MPs tell Lok Sabha Speaker NCPI move broke no constitutional rule
stories.dek: The 20 MPs filed individual replies on the last day of the deadline, countering disqualification petitions brought by Abhishek Banerjee under the Tenth Schedule.
stories.summary: Twenty breakaway Trinamool Congress MPs submitted replies to Speaker Om Birla on Tuesday, saying their move to the NCPI violated no constitutional provision. Abhishek Banerjee has petitioned for their disqualification under the anti-defection law.
body: Twenty rebel Trinamool Congress MPs who aligned with the NCPI have submitted replies to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, saying their exit from the party broke no parliamentary or constitutional provision, NCPI chief whip Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar said on Tuesday, November 24.

The replies were filed on the last day of the deadline set by the Lok Sabha Secretariat. They respond to disqualification petitions filed by Abhishek Banerjee, the TMC's national general secretary. Each MP submitted an individual reply of 17-18 pages, according to Ghosh Dastidar.
"We have joined the NCPI following all parliamentary and constitutional norms," she told PTI.

MP Arup Chakraborty said the breakaway was a collective decision taken after the TMC's defeat in the West Bengal Assembly elections. "We felt that if we had to sustain our organisation and retain people's respect, we needed to form a team," he said.

Chakraborty said the decision to support the BJP-led NDA came afterwards, as part of the group's political strategy. He rejected the charge of anti-party activity. "We are the majority group, and hope that the majority's position will be recognised," he said.

Sudip Bandyopadhyay, who leads the NCPI bloc in the Lok Sabha, said the replies rebutted Banerjee's allegations. Chakraborty also said a meeting with Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari could not be ruled out, given that the alliance operates nationally.

The TMC leadership has maintained that the rebels cannot escape the consequences of leaving the party by presenting their exit as a political realignment. Earlier, party leader Kunal Ghosh criticised the rebels' repeated requests for more time to reply.

The Lok Sabha Secretariat issued notices on August 26. The MPs sought extensions five times, saying they needed time to collate documents and prepare replies with their legal team. Chakraborty attributed the delays to festivals including Bhai Phonta, Kali Puja, Diwali and Durga Puja.

Official Lok Sabha records still list the MPs as TMC members, although they have sought recognition as a separate parliamentary formation. Whether a collective departure is protected under the anti-defection law will be examined under the Tenth Schedule.

The Supreme Court agreed on August 25 to hear Banerjee's plea seeking an expeditious decision from the Speaker. The Speaker must now examine the individual replies and the arguments of both sides before ruling on the petitions.
keyFacts: Twenty of the TMC's 27 Lok Sabha MPs broke away in June and aligned with the NCPI.
The Lok Sabha Secretariat issued notices to the MPs on August 26.
The rebels sought extensions five times before filing replies on November 24.
Each reply runs to 17-18 pages, according to Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar.
The Supreme Court agreed on August 25 to hear Abhishek Banerjee's plea for a speedy decision.
stories.background: The split followed the TMC's defeat in the West Bengal Assembly elections. It has extended to the Assembly, where around 60 of 80 TMC MLAs backed Ritabrata Banerjee's claim to the Leader of the Opposition's post. The Election Commission allotted the Mamata Banerjee-led faction the name Mamata All India Trinamool Congress and the Football Player symbol. The Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction received the name Democratic Trinamool Congress and the Envelope symbol.
stories.whyItMatters: The Speaker's decision will determine whether the 20 MPs keep their Lok Sabha seats and whether their group is recognised separately from the TMC.

stories.headline: Maharashtra panel proposes 7-10 year jail term, ₹10-crore fine for paper leaks
stories.dek: The committee headed by additional chief secretary V Radha also wants a special task force and fast-track courts, and Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis plans a bill in the winter session.
stories.summary: A Maharashtra reform committee has recommended a minimum ₹10-crore fine and seven to 10 years in jail for those guilty of exam paper leaks. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said the state will amend the law and try to table a bill in the winter session.
body: A seven-member committee set up by the Maharashtra government has recommended a minimum fine of ₹10 crore and a jail term of seven to 10 years for people found guilty of leaking competitive exam papers, with property to be seized.

The panel, headed by additional chief secretary V Radha, submitted its report to the state government on Monday. It proposes raising the minimum jail term from five years to seven. The current punishment for organised exam fraud under the Maharashtra Competitive Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 is five to 10 years. The report also specifies the property that can be seized: land, buildings, movable property, intellectual property and digital or virtual assets.

For candidates who use unfair means, the committee proposed a jail term of five to 10 years and a fine of up to ₹50 lakh. The existing penalty is three to five years and a fine of up to ₹10 lakh. It also recommended refunding exam fees, which range from ₹344 to ₹544, to all candidates whether or not they pass.

Service provider agencies involved in malpractice would face a penalty of ₹5 crore instead of ₹1 crore, recovery of exam-related expenses, and an eight-year ban instead of four. Directors and managers of such firms would face five to 10 years in prison and a ₹5-crore fine, against three to 10 years and ₹1 crore now.

The committee also proposed a Special Task Force to investigate exam offences and fast-track courts for speedy trials. Pending cases would move to these courts and be disposed of within three months. It suggested a three-tier Command Control Centre system at the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) headquarters, in districts and at exam venues, and one-time candidate registration through MahaID or Aadhaar.
Fadnavis said: “The state government will amend the present act and try to table a related bill in the upcoming winter session of the state legislature.”

BJP MLA Vikram Pachpute, who was part of a team coordinating with protesting students, welcomed the recommendations. “We are confident the state government will implement these reforms, which will prove a huge relief for students,” he said.
Radha said the committee will submit its final report in January 2027.
keyFacts: The committee was appointed on September 4 and submitted its second report on Monday.
Proposed minimum fine for paper leaks is ₹10 crore; minimum jail term rises from five to seven years.
Candidates using unfair means could face five to 10 years and fines up to ₹50 lakh.
Pending cases would go to fast-track courts and be decided within three months.
The final report is due in January 2027.
stories.background: The committee was appointed after the MPSC's March 22 exam for drug inspectors leaked, affecting thousands of candidates. A network of MPSC officials, a coaching institute and middlemen is suspected of involvement. MPSC aspirants protested in Pune earlier this year over alleged leaks, irregularities and recruitment delays. The panel's interim report on November 5 recommended raising MPSC Group C positions from 5,000 to more than 16,000.
stories.whyItMatters: If the amendments pass, penalties for organisers, candidates and service agencies in state competitive exams would rise sharply, and all candidates would get their fees refunded.

stories.headline: CSMT redevelopment deadline moves to December 2028 as RLDA says 30% work done
stories.dek: Rail Land Development Authority officials say the elevated concourse linking all 18 platforms has yet to begin, and platforms 14 and 15 will stay shut until January 31, 2027.
stories.summary: The deadline for redeveloping Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus has moved from mid-2026 to December 2028, RLDA officials said. Only 30% of the work is complete, and a revised cost estimate of ₹3,155.50 crore awaits railway ministry approval.
body: The deadline for redeveloping Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) in Mumbai has been pushed back by nearly 2.5 years, from mid-2026 to December 2028, according to officials of the Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA), which is executing the project.

RLDA officials said only 30% of the work is complete. Construction of an elevated concourse connecting all 18 platforms, a key component, has not yet started. They cited the need to disrupt suburban and long-distance services as little as possible, and additional work such as roofing over platforms, as reasons for the revised date.

"The complexity of undertaking redevelopment at an operational railway station is immense," an RLDA official said. The official pointed to the station's 18 platforms, daily footfall of over 600,000 and limited working space.

Work began in January 2023 with refurbishment of platforms used by long-distance trains. After platforms 16 and 17 were completed, platforms 14 and 15 were closed on October 1 for 75 days, until December 15. Central Railway officials said that date is now January 31, 2027, because roofing over the platforms was not in the original scope.

A senior Central Railway official, who asked not to be named, said some trains are being terminated on other platforms and some short-terminated at Dadar and Thane. "It is a big operational challenge as it impacts the overall punctuality of trains," the official said. Once work on platforms 14 and 15 ends, construction will move to platforms 10-13.

The platform work includes laying the foundation for a 122-metre-long, 67-metre-wide elevated concourse. The project also covers two new station buildings along P D'Mello Road, where RLDA officials said foundation work is under way. They acknowledged that construction activity, barricades and machinery often cause chaotic scenes outside the station.
The original contract value was ₹2,450 crore. A revised estimate of ₹3,155.50 crore is awaiting approval from the railway ministry, RLDA officials said.

Madhu Kotian, president of the Mumbai Rail Pravasi Sangh, said the delay was unfounded and was inconveniencing passengers. "Either the contractor is not being paid on time or there is a severe problem with availability of manpower," he said.

RLDA officials said such projects at major stations generally take 4-6 years. "The overall project timeline has been revised only once," an RLDA official said, adding that dates for individual components and phased commissioning should not be treated as repeated extensions of the whole project.
keyFacts: CSMT redevelopment deadline moved from mid-2026 to December 2028.
RLDA officials say 30% of the work is complete.

Revised cost estimate of ₹3,155.50 crore awaits railway ministry approval; original was ₹2,450 crore.
Elevated concourse will be 122 metres long and 67 metres wide.
stories.background: CSMT is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The project aims to create an airport-style multimodal transit hub, decongest platforms and upgrade amenities while preserving the heritage architecture. It covers about 450,000 square metres, including nearly 200,000 sqm of new construction and 250,000 sqm of redeveloped infrastructure.
stories.whyItMatters: Over 600,000 passengers use CSMT daily, and the continuing platform closures force some trains to terminate elsewhere, which Central Railway says affects punctuality.

stories.headline: BMC's fixed deposits fall to ₹79,873 crore; Congress seeks white paper
stories.dek: Congress leader Ashraf Azmi wants an account of withdrawals since 2021; civic officials say year-end dips in reserves are routine and funds are replenished.
stories.summary: The BMC's fixed deposits fell from ₹81,449 crore in February 2026 to ₹79,873 crore in October. Congress has demanded a white paper on withdrawals and spending, while civic officials say such dips are seasonal.
body: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's fixed deposits fell from ₹81,449 crore in February 2026 to ₹79,873 crore in October, and the Congress has demanded a white paper on how the money was withdrawn and spent, The Times of India reported.
The party wants the document to cover withdrawals from the deposits between 2021 and September 2026, how the funds were used, and whether the interest earned has been properly accounted for.

Congress leader Ashraf Azmi claimed the deposits have fallen by ₹11,818 crore since 2021-22. He alleged the BMC may have earned an estimated ₹5,000 crore a year in interest over five years. He also questioned how the civic body would meet liabilities of ₹2.44 lakh crore, including payments to contractors.

Civic officials said reserves usually dip towards the end of a financial year because several bills are paid and expenditure is incurred. They said this does not mean the reserves have fallen permanently, as funds are replenished through the year.
The officials also disputed the interest figure. They said interest on the deposits could be around ₹2,500 crore a year, not ₹5,000 crore.
BMC budget documents list reserves of ₹87,131 crore in 2022-23, ₹88,304 crore in 2023-24, ₹84,824 crore in 2024-25, ₹81,774 crore in 2025-26 and ₹81,449 crore in 2026-27.

The BMC says it has committed liabilities of ₹2,13,146 crore for priority infrastructure projects and ₹31,407 crore for essential works. The largest items include the Mumbai Coastal Road (North) project at ₹33,911 crore, the Mumbai Sewage Disposal Project at ₹22,916 crore and the Water Conveyance Tunnel at ₹17,469 crore.
Other listed projects are the Goregaon-Mulund Link Road at ₹15,738 crore, a 200 MLD desalination plant at ₹14,050 crore and cement concretisation of major roads at ₹12,257 crore.
keyFacts: BMC fixed deposits: ₹81,449 crore in February 2026, ₹79,873 crore in October 2026.

Officials put annual interest at about ₹2,500 crore, not ₹5,000 crore.
BMC lists committed liabilities of ₹2,13,146 crore for priority projects and ₹31,407 crore for essential works.

stories.whyItMatters: The deposits fund Mumbai's civic spending, and the BMC has large committed infrastructure liabilities, including payments to contractors.

stories.headline: Ramayana makes Oscars visual effects top 20; Disney leads with four films
stories.dek: Nitesh Tiwari's Indian epic joins The Odyssey and Dune: Part Three among 20 films advancing in the Academy's visual effects race, Variety reported.
stories.summary: Variety reported that 20 films, including the Indian epic Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, have advanced in the Oscars visual effects race. Disney leads the field with four titles; the Academy has not confirmed the list.
body: "Ramayana: Rise of a Legend", the Indian mythological epic starring Ranbir Kapoor, is among 20 films that have advanced in the visual effects category for the 99th Academy Awards, Variety reported on Tuesday, citing multiple sources.

The Academy's Visual Effects Branch notified the artisans behind the films ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, according to Variety. The Academy does not release the list publicly and declined to comment or confirm which films advanced.

Disney leads with four titles: "Avengers: Doomsday", "Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu", "Whalefall" and the live-action "Moana". Skydance has three, "Dune: Part Three", "Digger" and "Supergirl", though Variety said four of its other contenders fell short.

Sony also has three: "Ramayana: Rise of a Legend", "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" and "Jumanji: Open World". Universal has "The Odyssey" and "Disclosure Day", and Amazon MGM Studios has "Project Hail Mary" and "The Sheep Detectives".

Variety said "Ramayana" follows S.S. Rajamouli's "RRR", which reached the top 20 for the 95th Oscars. It described the inclusion as a sign of the branch's continued appetite for large-scale spectacle from outside Hollywood.

The rest of the list is "Backrooms" from A24, "Godzilla Minus Zero", "Heart of the Beast" from Paramount, "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" from Lionsgate, "The Mosquito Bowl" from Netflix and Laika's "Wildwood". Paramount's "Ebenezer" and "Street Fighter" did not make the cut, Variety said.

Preliminary voting for the shortlist runs from December 7 to December 11, and shortlists in all categories will be announced on December 15. The 10 shortlisted visual effects films will be presented to branch members on January 8-10. Nominations will be announced on January 21, and the ceremony is on March 14 at the Dolby Theatre.

stories.headline: Marathi film Gondhal and Naga drama Angh join Oscars international feature race
stories.dek: Both films are among 104 titles the Academy has declared eligible for the 2027 International Feature Film category, alongside Nepal's Elephants in the Fog.
stories.summary: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences on Tuesday listed Gondhal and Angh among 104 titles eligible for the International Feature Film category at the 2027 Oscars. Gondhal is India's official submission; Angh qualified through a Toronto festival award.
body: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences on Tuesday named Marathi film Gondhal and Nagaland-set drama Angh among 104 titles eligible for the International Feature Film category at the 99th Academy Awards, Hindustan Times reported.
Gondhal, directed by Santosh Davakhar, is India's official submission. Angh, from filmmaker Theja Rio, secured its place by winning the Platform Award at the Toronto International Film Festival.

According to a report by The Hollywood Reporter, cited by Hindustan Times, 100 of the films were submitted by individual countries and territories. Four others qualified through top prizes at major festivals. Besides Angh, they are Midday Meal (Busan Award for Best Film), Shame and Money (World Cinema Grand Jury Prize for Dramatic Film at Sundance) and Yellow Letters (Golden Bear at the Berlin International Film Festival).

Nepal's entry, Elephants in the Fog, is also on the list, as The Statesman noted in its headline. Other entries include Japan's All of a Sudden, Poland's Fatherland, Romania's Fjord, Spain's La Bola Negra, France's Minotaur, South Korea's Possible Love, the United Kingdom's Rehearsals for a Revolution and Pakistan's Hanging by a Wire.

Eligibility lets both Indian films compete in the preliminary round of voting. The Academy will later announce a shortlist, followed by the final nominations. Members from all branches can vote in the preliminary round if they meet minimum viewing requirements.
Under Academy rules, an International Feature Film must be a feature-length film produced outside the United States, with most of its dialogue in a language other than English.

Gondhal is set in rural Maharashtra and follows a single night against the backdrop of the traditional midnight Gondhal ritual, combining music, dance, mythology and religious traditions. Angh is set in 1960s Nagaland and follows an ageing Konyak village chief and his son, who are among the last trying to preserve their ancestral faith and way of life as change arrives around them.
The 99th Academy Awards will be held in 2027 at the Dolby Theatre at Ovation Hollywood.

stories.headline: Cine workers' body asks PM Modi to block Pakistani Netflix series Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo
stories.dek: Netflix released the trailer on November 24 and has not said whether the December 4 premiere will be available to viewers in India.
stories.summary: The All Indian Cine Workers Association has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking a stop to the Indian release of a Pakistani series starring Fawad Khan and Mahira Khan. Netflix has not said whether Indian subscribers will get it.
body: The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi asking that the Pakistani series Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo not be released or streamed on Netflix in India on December 4.

The two-page letter, dated November 24, is signed by AICWA president Suresh Shyamlal Gupta, Bollywood Hungama reported. It is also marked to Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and Netflix India. The association shared copies on its official X account on Tuesday.

AICWA listed four demands: that the series not stream in India on December 4 or later; that all OTT platforms comply strictly with the I&B ministry's advisory of May 8, 2025; that the government bring a permanent law with penalties restricting Pakistani content, artists and productions on television, streaming and cinema; and that Netflix India and other services state publicly their position on Pakistani-origin content.

The letter cites the 2019 Pulwama attack and the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam attack. The May 2025 advisory asked OTT platforms, streaming services and intermediaries to stop streaming Pakistani-origin content. AICWA argues that releasing the series goes against the spirit of that advisory.

According to The Times of India, the letter says the cast includes "people of a terrorist country who will never wish well for India" and claims some members have spoken against India during times of tension. The Times of India's account named Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan, Hania Aamir and Saman Ansari; Bollywood Hungama and Hindustan Times list Sanam Saeed in the cast. The sources do not identify which cast members AICWA means.
In its X post, AICWA said: "Pakistan was, is and will remain a terrorist country."

Netflix released the official trailer on November 24, Hindustan Times reported. The series is based on Farhat Ishtiaq's Urdu novel and is Netflix's first original series set in Pakistan. It follows six love stories across three generations. Ahad Raza Mir, Iqra Aziz, Hamza Ali Abbasi and Maya Ali are also in the cast. Momina Duraid directs and produces. It was filmed in Pakistan, Italy and the United Kingdom.
The series, titled All The Love Our Hearts Carry for international audiences, will come in two parts. Part 1 premieres on December 4, with Part 2 to follow.
As of November 24, the title appeared on Netflix India's website but not its app, according to Hindustan Times. Netflix has not issued a statement on availability in India.

AICWA says it had earlier barred Pakistani artistes from working in India after the 2019 Pulwama attack.
stories.whyItMatters: Indian subscribers may not be able to watch the series if Netflix or the government acts on the advisory, and the association is also seeking a permanent law on Pakistani content.

stories.headline: Puerto Rico's Jennifer Barreto wins Miss Universe 2026 on home soil
stories.dek: India's Kaziah Liz Mejo, 19, reached the top 30 at the 75th pageant but did not make the top 12.
stories.summary: Jennifer Barreto, 27, of Puerto Rico won the 75th Miss Universe title in her home country, crowned by Fatima Bosch of Mexico. India's Kaziah Liz Mejo, a law student from Kerala, was eliminated before the top 12.
body: Jennifer Barreto, 27, of Puerto Rico won the 75th Miss Universe pageant in her home country, receiving the crown from reigning titleholder Fatima Bosch of Mexico, Hindustan Times reported on Wednesday.

Barreto represented San Sebastián. Melissa Nunez of the Dominican Republic was named first runner-up, and Clara Vegas Goetz of Venezuela was second runner-up. The top five also included contestants from the Philippines and New Zealand.
The win is Puerto Rico's sixth Miss Universe crown, according to Hindustan Times.

In the final round, each finalist was asked, "What does the world need most from its leaders right now?" Barreto answered: "I believe the world needs leaders who are professionally empathetic. We live in a world where we often judge and question others, but a leader should stand up for their values, set an example, and raise the bar."

According to Halo, as cited by Hindustan Times, Barreto is married and has a 7-year-old daughter, Penélope. She holds master's degrees in psychology and clinical social work, and serves as a prevention specialist for the US Army Department of Defence.

India's Kaziah Liz Mejo, 19, made the top 30 but did not advance to the top 12. The top 12 were from Chile, the Dominican Republic, the United States, New Zealand, Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Philippines, Colombia, Nicaragua, Venezuela, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and France.

Mejo, a law student, classical dancer, public speaker and actor from Kerala, won the Miss Universe India 2026 title in August, becoming the first woman from Kerala to do so. She had competed against 52 finalists. In Puerto Rico she took part in the national costume round, themed on Kerala and Indian textile heritage, and in the swimsuit round.
The Miss Universe India grand finale was held in Jaipur. Organisers said around 8,000 to 9,000 aspirants were considered during selection.

stories.headline: Marvel plans tribute to Patrick Stewart in Avengers: Doomsday after his final day on set
stories.dek: Directors Anthony and Joe Russo say Stewart was visibly struggling with his health while filming, and Kevin Feige says the studio is working on how to honour him.
stories.summary: Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige and directors Anthony and Joe Russo told Entertainment Weekly that Patrick Stewart gave an emotional speech on his last day of filming. The studio is planning a tribute in Avengers: Doomsday, due in theatres on December 18.
body: Marvel Studios is planning a tribute to Patrick Stewart in Avengers: Doomsday, studio president Kevin Feige said, after the directors described an emotional final day of filming for the actor, who died last month.

Feige and co-directors Anthony and Joe Russo spoke to Entertainment Weekly. Feige said Stewart stood up and gave a speech to the crew on his last day. "We didn't know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was," Feige said.
Anthony Russo said the possibility was on everyone's mind. "It was in the back of all of our heads, we may never see him on set again," he said, calling the atmosphere "very emotional".

Russo said it was clear Stewart was struggling with his health. "He worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence — for us as directors, for his other actors, for the crew," he said. He added that Stewart's effort to deliver the performance made the experience "intensely emotional".

On the tribute, Feige said: "We're long done filming that movie, and he did an amazing job for us. We're looking now at how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend." No details of the planned tribute were given.

Stewart plays Charles Xavier, or Professor X, in the film for the ninth and final time. Joe Russo called Xavier "the conscience in the movie" and said he has a scene with Ian McKellen, Stewart's close friend, about forgiveness. "I think very resonant in the wake of his passing," Joe Russo said.
Variety, citing Entertainment Weekly, reported that Stewart had been offered a role in the sequel, Avengers: Secret Wars, due in December 2027, but declined.
Avengers: Doomsday opens in theatres on December 18.

stories.headline: U2 announce North American stadium dates for 2027 world tour
stories.dek: The Irish band will play 18 shows from August to October 2027, with the War on Drugs and Stephen Wilson Jr. as support acts.
stories.summary: U2 have added North American stadium dates, running from August to October 2027, to their Carnaval de Luz world tour. The War on Drugs and Stephen Wilson Jr. will share support duties across the continent.
body: U2 have announced a run of North American stadium shows from August to October 2027, adding to a tour behind their album Carnaval de Luz, Pitchfork reported on Tuesday.

The band will start in Miami at Hard Rock Stadium on August 13 and finish at BC Place in Vancouver on October 18. The tour is titled Carnaval de Luz Presents: The Greatest Show on Earth World Tour 2027.
Stephen Wilson Jr. will open the eastern leg, from Miami through Foxborough, Massachusetts. The War on Drugs will support on the later dates, from Arlington, Texas, onward.

The eastern dates include Atlanta (Mercedes-Benz Stadium, August 17), Baltimore (M&T Bank Stadium, August 20), and two nights at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on August 26 and 28. The band then plays Chicago's Soldier Field on September 3, two nights at Rogers Stadium in Toronto on September 7 and 9, and Gillette Stadium in Foxborough on September 14.

The western and southern leg begins at AT&T Stadium in Arlington on September 27. U2 then play SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles on October 1 and 2, Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on October 9, Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara on October 15, and BC Place in Vancouver on October 18.

The new dates follow earlier announcements for South America and Europe. In South America, Beck will support shows in Mexico City, São Paulo and Buenos Aires, with four nights in each city from February 23 to March 29.

The European leg, with Wolf Alice supporting, runs from April 26 in Stockholm to July 9 in Milan. It includes three nights at Stade de France in Paris, four at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, and two at Berlin's Olympiastadion.
